How the solution is held Both halves are Taskweft's own Elixir DSL, rendered by mix rfd.rectgtn from the RFD sources, and Taskweft.Compose.compose_strings/2 merges a pair so the planner compiles it into a solution. That solution renders into the RFD's DETAILS.md , and a gate holds it against what the planner returns. Where the declarations live A steps block inside an rfd block declares the critical path: steps do step "Build", repos: ["entities-godot", "the godot-sandbox addon"], missing: "the exported template_release build faults in a StringName copy", check: "an OpenXR session starts on each path and the pen scene draws in it", state: :failed end repos and check are required, because a step nobody owns and a step that ends at nothing are the two ways a critical path rots. missing is what the step needs that does not exist yet, control is the planted defect its check must catch, and state is where the step stands. A step declared parked states what it is missing, so parking is never silent. Why the Elixir DSL and not JSON-LD Taskweft reads a domain written in its own Elixir DSL, and Taskweft.Compose.compose_strings/2 composes DSL sources directly, so nothing here authors JSON-LD. Writing the first draft against the JSON-LD path found three defects in Taskweft.DSL.SafeParser , all one bug: a value went through to_string/1 . - An integer value: 1 reached the planner as the string "1" . - A negative literal raised Protocol.UndefinedError on its unary-minus AST, in an action body, a variable's init and an alternative's check . - A computed value: %{type: "math/add", ...} was dropped to {} or raised. The same bug had been fixed once before for a goal's eq , and the comment recording it is still in dsl_goal_test.exs . Six controls in dsl_value_type_test.exs cover the three sites now; five of them fail against the parser as it was. Where the antifragility is A failure makes the plan longer rather than making it fail. The step method's alternatives are already_checked , close_the_gap_first , parked_and_named , run_it , park_it , and a step the problem states as failed matches the second, which plans close-the-gap and then run-step . Measured over one four-step problem, changing only step 3's state: step 3 plan length what the planner adds ready , the control 7 nothing failed 8 close-the-gap before the retry parked 6 nothing, and step 3 is not run checked 6 nothing, and step 3 is not run again A system that merely survived the failure would have planned 7 again and retried the same step. RFD66606-2287 carries this today: its Build step is failed , so its solution is 12 steps and opens with the gap. What the gate measures scripts/check_rectgtn_plan.exs reads each RFD that declares steps, takes the solution its DETAILS.md renders, and asks the planner for the plan: Taskweft.Compose.compose_strings/2 over rectgtn/organization.ex and that RFD's problem, then Taskweft.NIF.plan/1 . A difference fails the command. elixir scripts/check_rectgtn_plan.exs 1/1 solutions are the planner's elixir scripts/check_rectgtn_plan.exs --self-test 14 controls Taskweft is a separate checkout, so the gate runs at the manual stage where a repo workspace exists, and a missing checkout is a FAIL rather than a skip. Fourteen controls cover the plan shape without it, including that a failure lengthens the plan and that a parked step naming nothing missing is refused. What this does not do The planner does no work; it names the next step. Nothing writes a step's state from a check run, so a step's state is a declaration a reader keeps honest, the same way a blocklist row is. One problem per RFD is rendered for all of them, and 360 of the 361 carry no steps, so their solutions are prepare , gate , open-pr , enqueue and say little. The shape is worth having before the second rung declares its path. Related RFD66606-2287 (the first rung) is the first problem; RFD66606-2204 (RECTGTN fleet coordination) plans over peers rather than documents; RFD66606-2232 (RFD authoring as an Elixir DSL) gives the build-artifact rule; RFD66606-2177 carries the flight levels the domain holds. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2292: the organization is one RECTGTN domain

b: State: discussion Feature: where an agent session keeps what it learns about V-Sekai-fire and chibifire-stages, and the operator's rules that lived in one desk's memory, written down Scope: this repository, CLAUDE.md , every agent session's local memory, and the rules below What any agent learns about V-Sekai-fire and chibifire-stages lives in an RFD, not a desk. An agent session's memory is a directory on one desk, so no session sees every rule. What any agent needs to know about V-Sekai-fire and chibifire-stages, their repositories, the headset and the services lives in an RFD in this repository: the RFD that owns the topic, or this one when none does. A desk's local memory keeps only what is true of that desk alone, such as its paths, its identities and its tools. A local note about a generic rule names the RFD that states it. Write a generic rule into its RFD in the same session; the sections below hold the steps. Writing a generic rule down An agent that learns a generic rule writes it into the RFD in the same session, through a pull request like any other change. What lived on one desk On 2026-10-01 the operator's rules for locomotion, offline deployment, video and the station lived only on the Mac desk, and those for where compute runs and for binary translation only on the Windows desks, so no session saw all of them. Starting out in the workspace A new agent, a small local model included, starts here and does one step at a time. It begins right after the bootstrap script has run. 0. The bootstrap leaves a workspace root holding .repo/ , AGENTS.md and the placed projects. Every path below is relative to that root. ls .repo and repo list confirm it. If repo , elixir , mix or python is missing, ask the operator; don't install tools yourself. 1. Read AGENTS.md at the workspace root, then this RFD. 2. The workspace is a repo client. .repo/manifests/default.xml (the taskweft manifest repository) places every project on a side of the hexagon: 2-contract/ , 3-interactor/ , 4-entities/ , 5-repository/ , 6-datasource/ , 7-service/ . repo list shows what is placed. 3. Sync with elixir .repo/manifests/sync.exs . --preflight first, then elixir .repo/manifests/sync.exs . . A project the preflight names as blocking gets a decision from the operator, not a guess. One that blocks because another session works in it moves its branch to a worktree, uncommitted edits carried by git stash , and then syncs (operator, 2026-10-18). 4. Never edit a placed checkout in place. Make a worktree in a scratch directory on a new dev/ branch: git -C worktree add / -b dev/ /main , using the project's own remote and default branch. 5. Commit subjects are sentence-case prose with no feat: prefix and no trailing period, forks included (RFD66606-2026). Commits and pull requests carry no Claude attribution: no Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer and no "Generated with Claude Code" line. Credit to people stays, such as a co-author trailer for the person whose work a commit carries. "Interchangeable sessions" below names the commit author and how to strip a footer a tool appends. Push only the feature branch, and open the pull request in V-Sekai-fire or chibifire-stages, where the operator merges it. 6. Remove the worktree when the pull request is open. An RFD is amended in rfd/NNNN-slug.exs of manuals-weftspun ( 2-contract/manuals-weftspun ), never in the rendered Markdown, which is a build artifact: 1. Find the RFD that owns the topic with grep -l rfd/ .exs . Use this one when none does. 2. Edit its decision or one of its details blocks in the tenseless present (RFD66606-2172). A statement that is no longer true is deleted, not retracted. Name the operator and date for an operator's decision. 3. A new RFD takes the next serial in SERIALS.exs and carries the sentence "This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped." 4. Run mix rfd.render , python scripts/check_tropes.py --base /main and python scripts/check-rfd-structure.py . All three pass before the push. 5. Keep product names and other organisations' issue or PR references out of the text, and cite an upstream change by its bare commit SHA. A worked example, typed into Git Bash on the Windows desk. It adds a sentence to this RFD: cd /2-contract/manuals-weftspun git fetch v-sekai-fire main git worktree add "$TEMP/rfd-edit" -b dev/rfd-my-topic v-sekai-fire/main cd "$TEMP/rfd-edit" Open rfd/2294-agent-knowledge-lives-in-rfds-not-in-desk-memory.exs , add the sentence inside the right details block, and save. Then: mix rfd.render python scripts/check_tropes.py --base v-sekai-fire/main python scripts/check-rfd-structure.py git commit -am "RFD66606-2294: say what the sentence makes true" git -c \ core.hooksPath=" /.repo/projects/2-contract/manuals-weftspun.git/hooks" \ push v-sekai-fire dev/rfd-my-topic gh pr create -R V-Sekai-fire/manuals-weftspun --base main --fill cd /2-contract/manuals-weftspun git worktree remove "$TEMP/rfd-edit" The push names the hooks directory by absolute path because a placed checkout's .git is a link into .repo/projects/ , which Git Bash cannot follow. Given the relative path, the pre-push hook dies before running its gates. Never skip the hook with --no-verify . With no GitHub credentials, stop after the commit and give the operator the branch name. When any step fails, stop and ask the operator rather than guess. The work queue The agent sessions share one work-stealing queue, the issues labelled worksteal on contract-zone-backend ( 2-contract/zone-backend ). Its protocol is pinned there as 58. An agent works its own queue newest first, and with nothing unclaimed steals the oldest unclaimed, unpinned issue from the fullest queue. A pinned issue needs one desk's hardware or credentials and is never stolen. The queue applies backpressure: a queue holding three or more open issues, pinned ones included, is full, its agent files nothing new and finishes first, a follow-up found mid-task becomes a checklist line in the issue that found it, and an operator request is still filed, with the queue's depth reported back so the operator can say what waits. Interchangeable sessions Any agent session, on a desk or in the cloud, can pick up any task another session started, because each follows the practices below and reads them here rather than from its own memory. A practice another RFD owns is named here and stated there. A desk's memory, a project's instructions, a skill or CLAUDE.md points at this section instead of restating it. - Attribution. Commits, pull requests, issue comments and reviews carry no agent credit: no agent Co-Authored-By trailer, no session link and no "Generated with" or "Generated by" footer. Commits are authored as K. S. Ernest (iFire) Lee . The GitHub connector and gh append a footer on create, so each body is rewritten with an update call and read back before the task moves on, and dot-claude 's hooks/strip_claude_footer.py prompts that rewrite after every create (operator, 2026-10-02). - Where a session posts. Pull requests, issues, comments, reviews and discussions go only to repositories in V-Sekai-fire and chibifire-stages. A fix to a fork lands in our fork, and nothing is sent upstream. Reading another organisation's code is fine (operator, 2026-10-05). - Automation. A new driver, gate or sheet builder is a plain Elixir script ( .exs ). Python appears only as a thin worker where a library has no other binding, such as Mitsuba's renderer. A cloud session runs the Elixir gates on CI's pinned toolchain, OTP 29 and Elixir 1.20.4 through erlef/setup-beam , never on a distribution's packaged Elixir (operator, 2026-10-02). - Where work runs. A cloud session has no GPU and takes CPU-only work: headless Godot gates, the godot-sandbox tests, CPU Mitsuba ( llvm_ad_rgb ), the cloth fit on its CPU backend, and blend-shape matching through contract-lbfgsb ( 2-contract/lbfgsb ). Its testing blocklists software GPU emulators: lavapipe and llvmpipe, SwiftShader, WARP, and Vulkan or Metal emulation. Work that needs a GPU (the persona, XR and headset runs, compute-rd and ggml runs, GPU sheet renders, macOS binaries) goes to the GPU desk rather than to an emulator. Timings are reported with milliseconds per frame (operator, 2026-10-02). - GPU Cloud and GPU-Free Cloud. Work split between the GPU desk's session ("GPU Cloud") and a cloud session ("GPU-Free Cloud") is one checklist in one issue, as on contract-zone-backend 114 . Each session ticks only its own items and comments when it starts, finishes or is blocked on one, with times in RFD66606-2295's form. Neither takes the other's items. - Branches. Every branch a session works on starts with a stage: dev/ , beta/ , rc/ or release/ , and archived/ once its work is parked or superseded, whatever name the session was handed (operator, 2026-10-12). No feat/ , fix/ , wip/ , main/ or bare names. - Capability-scoped workers. A worker session holds the capabilities its task needs as RFD66606-2200 tuples, and default deny covers the rest. A peer's request never widens a worker's rows. - Contact sheets. Release contact sheets are videos: the sphere_hammersley_sequence views are the columns and the fitting sequence is the frames. A CI job that shows a sheet renders it in that job and uploads it with actions/upload-artifact , so the sheet belongs to the run and the commit that made it. The colour reference is the lookdev-24 chart, entities-sakuragaoka-station ( 4-entities/sakuragaoka-station )'s tools/calib/chart24.json , and no commercial chart's trademark appears in code or documents. RFD66606-2370 holds the cell layout. - Characters. A garment is fitted to a character's body meshes only, and a character's own clothing is not loaded beneath it unless the operator asks for layering. Maro is the dress-on statue a garment is drawn onto. Mire is the avatar (operator, 2026-10-02). - Replies. RFD66606-2295 owns their form: the calibrated confidence tag, ISO 8601 times and intervals, and the known-unknown questions that close a plan. - Outcomes. Every script, gate and helper reports each outcome as an Elixir-shaped term on a line of its own: {:ok, %{...}} , or {:error, :reason_atom, %{...}} with the facts a reader needs to act. Nothing exits silently: a non-zero exit with no term is a defect, and so is an :ok path that prints nothing. Machine output a caller parses (a host name, a token) goes to stdout bare and the term goes to stderr (operator, 2026-10-16). On 2026-10-16 bao-active-host exited 1 with no output when every tailnet instance was a standby, which hid where the leader was. scripts/check_practices.exs checks what a file or the GitHub API can show: a commit authored or committed as the agent identity, a commit subject that is not sentence-case prose (RFD66606-2026), agent credit in a commit message, a pull request body, a comment or a review, a software GPU emulator in a workflow, a workflow that renders a contact sheet without uploading an artifact, and a branch that does not start with a stage. Its self-test carries a control in each direction for each check. It is defined once, as the practices hook in this repository's .pre-commit-hooks.yaml . Another repository lists that hook in its .pre-commit-config.yaml , where it runs on push, and its CI calls .github/workflows/practices.yml from here, which runs the same hook. Both pin a commit of this repository. This repository runs it as the ci-practices hook. Comments posted after the last run are seen at the next push or edit. The other practices hold by agreement. Merging An agent merges its own pull requests on V-Sekai-fire once they are green, through the merge queue where the repository has one. Where a repository requires no checks, --auto merges at once with its checks red, so there the agent waits for green and merges by hand. An agent may merge with the admin override (operator, 2026-10-30). The ban on it is rescinded. Bao and the tokens it mints Bao runs as tailnet nodes named weftspun-bao-N , and a desk uses whichever is online, keeping weftspun-bao.internal as the TLS server name. A desk logs in with its certificate, passing no role name , so the certificate selects the role. The login token is reused until its TTL lapses. A GitHub token is minted from github/token by the desk's git credential helper on each request, never printed or stored. No token is revoked: each one expires on its own within the hour (operator, 2026-10-03). Agents may use Bao to pass data to each other. What is written there is stored in S3 for 30 days and then rolled over (operator, 2026-10-01): Bao's storage is FoundationDB, whose backup goes to R2 (RFD66606-2143). An entry deleted from Bao stays in that copy until it rolls over. The problem A rule changed on one desk disagreed with the others without anyone being told. The tuples rebac rfd-2294--provides--agent-knowledge-in-rfds rfd-2294--is-a--workspace-policy Related - RFD66606-2200, the desk agent's ReBAC rows. - RFD66606-2363 to RFD66606-2381 and RFD66606-2413 to RFD66606-2419, the rules this RFD held before the split, one RFD each. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2294: agent knowledge lives in RFDs, not in desk memory

b: State: committed Feature: an agent tags every unverified claim with a word and a probability, (likely, p=0.80) , from one fixed scale Scope: agent replies to the operator, logbook entries, the times and closing questions in both, and scripts/check_confidence_tags.py An unverified claim carries its confidence as a word and a probability. Agent replies stated forecasts and diagnoses in the same voice as checked facts. A reader cannot weigh a claim that does not say how sure it is. A claim an agent has not verified carries its confidence as a word and a probability in one tag: (likely, p=0.80) . The word comes from a fixed scale of five, and the number must fall inside that word's band. A verified fact (a command's output, a merged pull request, a passing gate) carries no tag. scripts/check_confidence_tags.py reads the bands from this RFD's source and fails any tag whose word and number disagree, so the scale and the gate cannot drift apart. Run scripts/check_confidence_tags.py to check that each tag's number fits its word. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped. The scale The gate reads this table. A tag's number must lie inside its word's band, lower bound inclusive and upper bound exclusive, except that almost certain includes 1.00. word lower upper remote 0.00 0.10 unlikely 0.10 0.40 even 0.40 0.60 likely 0.60 0.90 almost certain 0.90 1.00 The tag The form is (word, p=0.NN) : the word, a comma, p= and the probability with two decimals. It follows the claim it qualifies: The walker stays bit-deterministic (likely, p=0.75). The 12 modules finish today (unlikely, p=0.25). Only unverified claims carry a tag. A claim the agent checked in the same turn states the check instead of a probability, because a probability on a checked fact would hide that it was checked. Calibration The numbers mean something only if they are calibrated: of the claims tagged p=0.80 , about four in five should turn out true. A logbook entry that records tagged forecasts also records how they resolved, so the tags can be scored. No such score exists yet; the first logbook entry to carry tagged forecasts starts it. Times A time in a reply, a logbook entry, an issue comment or a pull request is written in ISO 8601 with its date and UTC offset: 2026-10-02T09:51-07:00 , not 09:51 or 11am . A forecast's deadline is the same kind of time, so tagged by 2026-10-02T11:00-07:00 is scorable by a reader in another zone or on another day. A piece of work is timed as an ISO 8601 interval, start and end, followed by its duration (operator, 2026-10-02): 2026-10-02T20:12:48+00:00/2026-10-02T20:40:10+00:00, PT27M22S . Work still running gives its start and open . No gate checks this yet; it holds by agreement. Known unknowns A plan or a recommendation ends with zero to four questions about the known unknowns whose answers would change it, each answerable in one word with the recommended option marked. None are asked when nothing is unknown, and never more than four (operator, 2026-10-02). Replies are not files, so this holds by agreement. Related Lin, Hilton and Evans, "Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words" (2022, DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2205.14334, registered with DataCite) is the method: a model states its confidence in words and numbers, and the statement is scored for calibration. RFD66606-2294 (agent knowledge lives in RFDs) is why the rule is here and not in a desk's memory. CLAUDE.md 's "How Work Is Verified" rule 3 (a silent skip reads like a pass) is why a verified fact and a guess must look different. What is checked scripts/check_confidence_tags.py scans logbook/ .md and every RFD source for tags, and fails a tag whose word is not on the scale or whose number falls outside the word's band. Its self-test plants one tag of each kind, a correct one, an unknown word and a number outside its band, and asserts the gate passes the first and fails the other two. Replies are not files, so the gate cannot see them; the rule holds there by agreement. The problem On 2026-10-02 a reply described a Metal shader port as "Slang-to-MSL" when the shaders were hand-written, and the operator caught it. A bare percentage reads as code rather than as language.
t: RFD66606-2295: agent replies state calibrated confidence

b: State: committed Feature: XR Pilot keeps the runtime's PyroWave packets as they arrive and a separate step decodes them on an idle GPU into a CineForm intermediate Scope: XR Pilot and its MCP server, the pyro2cfhd and frames2cfhd tools, the CineForm SDK build, and the av1mkv delivery of a recording A recording keeps the runtime's own video stream and encodes it later on an idle GPU. Encoding live on the VR GPU would compete with the compositor, which an overload had already killed twice that day. A recording is the runtime's own video stream, not a screen capture. The pilot appends each PyroWave packet to a .pwrec file with its presentation and receive times and does no encoding while VR runs. A one-shot job later decodes the packets on the GPU that is not driving VR and encodes CineForm on the CPU. The CineForm file is the intermediate the delivery step wraps as MKV with a .cff (operator, 2026-10-09). The shared desk is run as the open work below records. Superseded by nut-based ffmpeg recording Recording moved to nut-based ffmpeg and works, so this RFD is committed (operator, 2026-11-11). The .pwrec and CineForm steps below are the earlier design and stay as history. The packet file .pwrec starts with the magic PWREC , two zero bytes and a version byte. Each frame is a u64 presentation time in ns, a u64 receive time in ns, a u32 index, a u32 byte count and the payload, at most 256 MiB. A pilot that restarts writes the next file with .1.pwrec . xr-pilot --record-stream and the MCP server's --record-stream write it. The decode step pyro2cfhd takes --fps , --size , --quality and --gpu (a PCI vendor and device pair). It runs as a one-shot task on the GPU without VR. frames2cfhd does the same from PNG frames. Both share one fit and RIFF writer. - The CineForm RIFF file stops at 4 GB. - The MKV writer built with llvm-mingw fails past 2 GB. - Full-rate 4K therefore needs a container writer fix before it ships. Building CineForm with MSVC Two changes let the CineForm SDK build with MSVC on the desk: simd_compat.h includes malloc.h for the aligned allocators, which MSVC has in place of mm_malloc.h ; lutpath.cpp declares its registry value name LPCTSTR , so string literals assign to it under strict strings. The llvm-mingw build of av1mkv needs the toolchain's libc++ and libunwind DLLs beside it, or it exits with 0xc00004bc. Motion that does not stutter Walking was integrated in the 60 Hz window loop while the tracking sender ran at a fixed 90 Hz, so one packet in three repeated a pose. The sender now runs at the runtime's announced refresh rate, clamped to 60 to 144 Hz, and moves held keys by real elapsed time; the window applies mouse look only. The wheel scales walk speed by 1.25 per notch, from 0.25 to 8 m/s; with Shift it moves the hand's reach. A 3D head gizmo draws yaw and pitch as arcs, so a trace shows when the head looks straight up or down. Open work - Run the pyro2cfhd self-test on the desk's second GPU, then record a real two-minute stream and deliver it. - Count compositor sync timeouts in the driver and give the sparklines fault thresholds, set from the sweep this RFD records. The problem The first two-minute sweep was saved as left-eye PNG frames and encoded at 10 fps, because a full-rate 4K clip passes the size limits of the CineForm RIFF writer and of the MKV writer built with llvm-mingw. Related - RFD66606-2303, the XR requirements; RFD66606-2365, the recording rules. - RFD66606-2306, operating the shared desk; RFD66606-2302, the frame budget. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2307: recording the xr pilot stream to cineform

b: State: committed Feature: each card serves Ternary Bonsai 2 27B through ninfer-all with a DFlash2 drafter of five tokens, and this RFD is how to set that up again from nothing on any Fedora 44 host Scope: the V-Sekai-fire/ninfer-all fork, the t2 .ninfer artifact, one systemd unit per card on Fedora 44 (native or WSL2), the mTLS front and the client's single router port Each card serves Bonsai 2 through ninfer-all with a DFlash2 drafter, set up from nothing. No RFD decided how a card serves Bonsai 2, and the setup lived in agents' notes, tied to whichever machine held the cards that week. A Bonsai 2 language server is ninfer-all serving the t2 bonsai2-27b-heretic.ninfer artifact with --spec dflash2 --draft-tokens 5 , one server per card, each a systemd unit on Fedora 44, native or in WSL2. Each server binds loopback only and takes an API key. stunnel with mutual TLS is the only way in from off the host. Clients reach every server through one router port. Fedora 44 is the only supported OS (operator, 2026-10-17). Build the engine and the host as the sections below say, then run the witnesses. The choice The operator chose the engine and drafter on 2026-10-12 ("The ninfer with dflash won") after the A-B-A run in the details. Blocklist - BLOCKLIST.md, "Speculative decoders other than MTP-3" and "1-bit PTQ1_0 bodies", both for the ggml language server. Sources Drafted on 2026-10-12 from an A-B-A run on one RTX 4090. Rewritten on 2026-10-17 to describe the setup rather than the machines it ran on, after the operator unshipped the fork's Windows support and kept Fedora 44, native or WSL2. The measurement One RTX 4090, the same launcher flags on every arm ( --max-context 262144 , --kv-dtype rk8v4 , --vision , one request at a time), three repetitions, temperature 0, 512 generated tokens, speeds read from the server's own timings . Arms ran A-B-A so the repeated arm shows drift. Decode in tokens per second: Arm chat code story ninfer-all, DFlash2 K=5 218-232 314-360 176-187 prebuilt engine, MTP-3 206-226 279-282 176-184 ninfer-all, MTP-3 193-206 239-267 164-172 - Prefill on ninfer-all is about 10% faster at 3k prompt tokens. - Story is a tie inside the spread. ninfer-all with MTP-3 is the slowest arm, so the gain needs both the engine and the drafter. - Temperature-0 text differs between the two engines and between the two drafters inside ninfer-all. - The prebuilt engine cannot run DFlash2 on this artifact without --lm-head-draft , and with it DFlash2 was slower than its MTP-3 on every workload. The artifact bonsai2-27b-heretic.ninfer , format t2_g128_fp16 , with the vision tower, the MTP head and the DFlash2 head inside it. The converter is pure Python and runs on the CPU, with recipe bonsai2_27b_ternary from the Heretic PQ2_0 body and the Bonsai-trained MTP and DFlash2 heads. The four sources and the artifact are published in the public dataset chibifire/ninfer-bonsai2-heretic (operator, 2026-10-12), with a sha256 to check a download against. Every input is Apache-2.0: Qwen3.8-27B, Ternary Bonsai 2 27B, the Heretic v2 modification, the MTP and DFlash2 heads and the weights they adapt. The dataset carries their licence and notice files, a root NOTICE that names each author and states the conversion, and an Apache-2.0 card. A published artifact names no host path. A workflow in the fork converts on a clean runner and fails on any of the runner's directories in the artifact or its report, after a planted path is caught. The prebuilt engine reads only t5_g128_fp16 , and ninfer-all reads only t2_g128_fp16 . An artifact from one family does not load in the other. The artifact cannot take --lm-head-q6 ; with it the server exits at startup. Building the engine v-sekai/build.nu in the fork builds on Fedora 44, native or WSL2, inside the fork's pixi build environment, which carries the compilers, CUDA, git, strip and gh. The host needs only curl to fetch pixi; git runs through pixi exec . The output is dist/linux (the programs and their library closure) and dist/tools-linux/ninfer-install . - One build compiles for one CUDA architecture; CMake refuses a list. - An sm_86 build runs on an RTX 3090 and an RTX 4090, so one build serves both cards of a two-card host. - In WSL2 the build drops the Windows entries from PATH , because CMake's package search over the 9p bridge takes minutes per lookup. The host layout - /opt/ninfer/bin and /opt/ninfer/lib come from dist/linux and are checked against its SHA256SUMS . /opt/ninfer/models holds the artifact, checked against the dataset's sha256. - A system user ninference runs the servers. The key is NINFER_API_KEY= in /etc/ninfer/env , root-only, read by systemd. - One unit per card, ninfer-serve- .service , enabled, restarting on any exit. It sets CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID and picks the card with --device , adds /opt/ninfer/lib to the library path (and /usr/lib/wsl/lib in WSL2), and runs: ninfer-serve /opt/ninfer/models/bonsai2-27b-heretic.ninfer --device --host 127.0.0.1 --port --api-key ${NINFER_API_KEY} --model-id bonsai-27b --max-context 262144 --kv-capacity 262144 --kv-dtype rk8v4 --vision --max-concurrency 1 --spec dflash2 --draft-tokens 5 --no-thinking - The binary takes the key only on its command line, so a shell on the host sees it in /proc , ps and systemctl status . Mask --api-key whenever processes or units are listed. - In WSL2 the distribution stops when no Windows process holds it, and its units stop with it. A logon task keeps one process running in it. Reaching it stunnel accepts on the host's tailnet address, one port per card, and forwards to the server's loopback port. It requires a client certificate under the chibifire Root and agent CA, and checks the client's host name against an allowlist. Its own certificate comes from RFD66606-2319. In WSL2 the tailnet address belongs to Windows, so stunnel runs there and forwards to the loopback port that WSL2 forwards into the distribution. On the client, a stunnel client maps each server to a local port, and a LiteLLM proxy ( v-sekai/router/ in the fork) puts all of them behind one port and one key. Its bonsai model goes to the least busy live server and skips one that is down; a name per card selects one server. Hermes calls only the router. Witnesses Each one carries a control that must fail. - Ready. GET /v1/models through the tunnel returns 200 with the key, and 401 without a key and with a wrong one. - Spec. The unit's command line, key masked, carries --spec dflash2 --draft-tokens 5 , and the server log reports draft acceptance above zero. - Vision. v-sekai/vision_zero_shot_probe.py against the tunnel names the red circle, the blue square and the text 42. A text-only server returns an error on the same request. - mTLS. The allowlisted client gets an HTTP answer. No certificate, and a certificate for a second client under the same CA, are both refused, the second with a subject-check failure. - Answer. The same temperature-0 code prompt gives the same answer hash on a rerun and after a reinstall on the same card. - Speed. Three reps of a 512-token code answer at temperature 0 land inside the card's previous runs. A number without that baseline is not reported. Pitfalls - Check that the files the running server holds still exist before a restart. A server keeps serving from a deleted model file, and the restart then fails with startup failed inspecting artifact . - CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID changes which card a device index names. Read nvidia-smi in the same order before choosing --device ; a build for a newer architecture fails on an older card with no kernel image . - Wait for the ready line listening on with a journal cursor taken before the restart, not with a timestamp. - An A/B that swaps --spec restores the unit in the same script on failure, because a server that dies at startup leaves its card down. Open questions - The decider benchmark behind the MTP-3 blocklist row has not been run on ninfer-all. Until it is, the row and this RFD measure different workloads, and neither says which drafter makes better decisions. - MTP's upstream advantage is a second request lane ( --max-concurrency 2 ). Every arm here served one request at a time. - DFlash2 at six and seven draft tokens is measured on one card only. - The unit and stunnel files are written by hand on each host and are in no repository. The problem Every move of the cards rebuilt it by hand. Related - RFD66606-2308 (Mac ninfer port), which uses this server as its reference. - RFD66606-2319 (endpoint certificates), where the front's certificate comes from. - RFD66606-2310 (eye-landmark scorer), which calls this server. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2311: serving bonsai 2 with ninfer-all and dflash2

b: State: committed Feature: a release tag is the Go pseudo-version of the commit it points at, so every tag sorts by time in a file listing and parses as a version in every package tool Scope: release tags in the V-Sekai-fire and chibifire-stages repositories, cut from 2026-10-13 on, and scripts/check_release_tags.exs A release tag is computed from its commit, so it sorts by time and parses everywhere. The orgs' releases carry four naming schemes and no rule. No single scheme among them sorts by time in a file listing and also parses as a version in Mix, Cargo, npm and Go. A release tag is v0.0.0- - : the tagged commit's committer time in UTC as YYYYMMDDhhmmss , then the first 12 hex digits of the commit. It is the shape of a Go pseudo-version, and it is computed from the commit, never typed. The core stays v0.0.0 . A stage, a rung name or a "1.0" goes in the release title and the stage branch, not in the tag. The operator chose the form on 2026-10-12 ("I like go's"). Run elixir scripts/check_release_tags.exs to recompute every tag, and read below for the later parts. The three parts The tag is the first of three parts of one release system. Each part does one job: identity is a hash, order is a fixed-width UTC time, stage is a pointer that moves, and compatibility is a version on the interface that breaks. The details give the later parts. Sources Drafted on 2026-10-12 from the release inventory, the sort runs and the parser runs below, all taken the same day. The form and the "everywhere" bar are the operator's. What a tag has to satisfy The operator's bar: a tag sorts in filesystem order, and the same string works everywhere a version is read. Measured on 2026-10-12, each candidate through each tool's own parser: Candidate ls order Mix Cargo npm Go v2026.01.05 , padded calendar date yes no no no no v2026.1.5 , unpadded calendar date no yes yes yes yes v1.0.0-beta.1 and v1.0.0 no yes yes yes yes v0.0.0-20261012203512-50cc405a1b2c yes yes yes yes yes - SemVer forbids a leading zero in a number, so a padded month fails every package tool. Unpadded, 2026.10.12 sorts before 2026.9.1 . - No file listing puts a release after its own pre-releases: ls , sort -V and Finder all list v1.0.0 before v1.0.0-beta.1 . - The Go form carries the date inside one alphanumeric pre-release field, where SemVer allows the zeros. ls , sort -V and Finder each put samples from January, October, the next day and the next year in time order. - Python's PEP 440 rejects the Go form. A Python package from the same commit is 0.0.0.devYYYYMMDDhhmmss . Docker's tag grammar admits the form; no Docker daemon ran in the measurement. What others do Read off the live registries on 2026-10-12. Builds between releases put an ISO basic date inside the pre-release: TypeScript 7.1.0-dev.20261012.1 , React 19.3.0-canary-9f2e1f88-20261012 , Node.js v27.0.0-nightly202610123b639be3a4 , Go v0.0.0-20261011100332-faecfb24eb49 . Calendar versions that must stay SemVer drop the padding: pip 26.2.1 , Home Assistant 2026.10.1 . Projects that list versions as strings pad instead: the Arch Linux ISOs, YYYY.0M.0D since 2012. Only Go's form, whose core never moves, sorts as plain bytes and parses as SemVer at once. The check scripts/check_release_tags.exs recomputes every tag from its commit: elixir scripts/check_release_tags.exs [ ] elixir scripts/check_release_tags.exs --self-test A tag on a commit from before 2026-10-13 is legacy, counted and named rather than failed; renaming a published tag breaks whatever points at it. The self-test plants six tags in a scratch repository. The commit's own pseudo-version passes; a seven-digit hash, a local-time stamp, a v1.0.0 core, a padded calendar date and a stage-suffixed date each fail by name; a pre-cutover tag reads as legacy. Go's own module.IsPseudoVersion accepts a seven-digit hash, so the 12-digit rule is this check's, not Go's. Go does hold a pseudo-version to its commit's time and hash, which is why the tag is computed: TZ=UTC git log -1 --format='v0.0.0-%cd-%h' \ --date=format-local:%Y%m%d%H%M%S --abbrev=12 The later parts Each part starts once the one before it runs. 1. The tag, this RFD. 2. The stage is a pointer. A moving tag per stage ( dev , beta , rc , release ) names the build that stage holds. Promotion moves the pointer to the same commit; nothing is rebuilt or renamed. The GitHub pre-release flag follows the pointer. 3. One release record per repository, and every other format derived from it. The Godot engine already works this way: version.py holds major, minor, patch and status; the build adds the commit hash and committer timestamp from git; the Windows resource takes FILEVERSION from the numbers; the Android build turns the status into a digit of versionCode (dev 1, alpha 2, beta 3). Here the record is the repository's CITATION.cff (operator, 2026-10-12), in two halves. The committed file holds what does not change per build: title, authors, licence, the interface versions. A commit cannot carry its own hash, so the release step writes the per-build half into the copy that ships with the artifact: version is the tag, commit the full hash, date-released the UTC date. CFF 1.2.0 admits no other top-level key; a status key fails its schema. The stage, the derived forms and the artifact digests ride as identifiers of type other : stage:dev , windows:YYYY.MMDD.hhmm.0 , android: , pep440:0.0.0.devYYYYMMDDhhmmss , sha256: . A sample of that shape validates against the CFF 1.2.0 JSON schema. The check recomputes every derived value from the commit field. 4. Compatibility rides on the interface that breaks: a protocol, ABI or save-format version that moves only when that interface does, as Go moves a module path to /v2 . 5. A signed attestation binds the record to the artifact's digest. The problem Of 60 GitHub releases in repositories pushed since 2026-06-01, 33 are SemVer pre-releases in at least four spellings, 7 are dates, 2 are plain SemVer and 18 are free names. Related - RFD66606-2294, interchangeable sessions: the stage branches this RFD leaves the stage to. - RFD66606-2295, calibrated replies: the times here are UTC, as there. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2312: release tags are go pseudo-versions

b: State: discussion Feature: Bao's storage stays the same size whatever the number of users, sessions or requests Scope: weftspun-bao on weftspun-fdb, every secrets engine and auth method mounted on it, and the plugins built for it Bao stays the same size however many users, sessions or requests arrive. Bao's default is to keep a lease for every dynamic secret, so an engine on the defaults grows with its traffic until a write fails. - Bao stores keys, configuration, policies and ReBAC tuples, and nothing that grows with users, sessions or requests (operator, 2026-10-13). - An engine that issues a credential per request keeps no lease and no record of it. The credential carries its own expiry and is never revoked. - Application data lives outside Bao, in the service that owns it. - Every engine ships a growth gate: issuing many credentials leaves the engine's storage unchanged, and a control that stores each one fails it. Read RFD66606-2317 next, the first engine held to this rule. Why the limit is part of the design FoundationDB refuses a value over 100,000 bytes and a transaction over 10,000,000 bytes, so the limit is part of the design and not a setting. Sources Written on 2026-10-13 from the operator's note that Bao has a hard data limit by design. The FDB backend was read in our OpenBao fork: Put calls one Set with the whole encrypted entry and splits nothing. The value and transaction limits are FoundationDB's published known limits. Neither limit has been measured on our cluster yet; the first engine's end-to-end test writes an entry just under and just over 100,000 bytes and records which one FDB refuses. What may be stored An entry belongs in Bao when the count of such entries is set by the operator, not by traffic: - signing keys, CA keys and certificates of issuers; - engine and mount configuration; - policies, cert roles and ReBAC tuples; - one-off secrets an operator puts there, such as an API token. These do not belong in Bao: - a lease or record per issued credential; - sessions, messages, counters, logs or audit trails of a service; - files and blobs of any size. An engine that needs to hold a resource for a while, such as a slot in a shared cap, may still use a lease, because the number of leases is capped by the resource and not by traffic. Its growth gate then checks that the lease count stays at or under the cap. The growth gate Each engine's unit tests run against logical.InmemStorage and count its keys with a recursive List before and after issuing 1,000 credentials. The gate passes when the count and the summed value size are unchanged. The control flips the engine to store each credential and must fail the same gate. The end-to-end test does the same against a dev server and also checks that the response carries no lease id. The problem Bao's storage is FoundationDB on three small machines, and the FDB backend writes each entry as one FDB value. Related - RFD66606-2140, Bao on FDB. - RFD66606-2353, Bao runs three replicas on the FDB machines. - RFD66606-2200, ReBAC agent roles. - RFD66606-2317, the first engine held to this rule. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2316: Bao holds a bounded set

b: State: committed Feature: a host that serves on the tailnet gets a server certificate for its own agent identity, signed by Bao's agent CA v2 without the root token Scope: weftspun-bao's pki-agents and pki-agents-v2 mounts, the csr-signer policy, and every stunnel or edge endpoint that serves under an agent identity A serving host gets its tailnet server certificate from agent CA v2, with no root token. Bao has two agent CAs, and nothing said which one does what. Bao signs a certificate in pki-agents that names the tailnet host anyway, and every client then rejects it. A host that serves takes a second certificate for its agent name from the pki-agents-v2 mount, through role agent-endpoint . That role sets server and client use, allows .agents.weftspun , .stonecat-ratio.ts.net and tailnet addresses, caps a certificate at 90 days and stores no record of it. The csr-signer policy may sign through it, so an agent identity issues an endpoint certificate without the root token. The key is made on the host and never leaves it. Read below for the mounts and the agent-endpoint role. What failed pki-agents holds the agent CA, whose name constraints allow only chibifire.com and agents.weftspun . On 2026-10-16 a server certificate for the Linux 4090 host failed this way. Sources Read on 2026-10-16 from the live cluster through the active weftspun-fdb machine: each mount's CA certificate and name constraints, the csr-signer policy, and the issuers on pki-agents . The Authority Information Access field of the Mac's own server certificate named pki-agents-v2 , which is how that mount was found. The mounts - pki-agents : issuer chibifire.com agent CA, constrained to chibifire.com and agents.weftspun . An agent signs with agent-client : client use only, 1 year. - pki-agents-v2 : issuer chibifire.com agent CA v2, constrained to the two above, stonecat-ratio.ts.net and 100.64.0.0/10 . An agent signs with agent-endpoint (this RFD). - pki : issuer Intermediate CA v2, no constraints read. No agent role; its key is unreadable on the node. - pki-listener : issuer bao listener CA, constrained to Bao's own names. Bao's listener only. Every issuer chains to the chibifire.com Root CA, so a client that trusts the Root ( ~/.bao.d/server-ca.pem on the Mac) verifies both agent CAs. The role pki-agents-v2/roles/agent-endpoint allowed_domains agents.weftspun,stonecat-ratio.ts.net allow_subdomains true allow_ip_sans true enforce_hostnames true server_flag true client_flag true use_csr_sans true ttl, max_ttl 2160h no_store true With no_store , Bao keeps no copy and cannot revoke the certificate. Each one expires within 90 days, which is the revocation (RFD66606-2316). The login certificate an agent already holds stays as it is; the endpoint certificate is a second one for the same name. Issuing one 1. On the host, make a P-256 key and a request whose config file carries extendedKeyUsage=serverAuth,clientAuth and the subject names: the agent name, the host's stonecat-ratio.ts.net name and its tailnet address. 2. Copy only the request off the host. An agent signs it with pki-agents-v2/sign/agent-endpoint under its own cert login. 3. Install the leaf with agent CA v2 after it as the full chain, and leave the Root out of the chain. Witnesses - Chain. openssl verify -purpose sslserver of the leaf against the Root, with agent CA v2 as the untrusted intermediate, prints OK. The same request signed on pki-agents fails with error 47, permitted subtree violation. - Use. A client-only agent-client leaf fails the same check with error 26, unsupported certificate purpose. - Signer. bao token capabilities pki-agents-v2/sign/agent-endpoint under an agent cert login returns create and update. The first two controls were run on 2026-10-16 and failed as planted, and the passing case ran the same day on the certificate below. What went wrong first On 2026-10-16 the role was written on pki-agents , the mount the client role lives on. It signed a certificate for the Linux host that failed error 47, and that certificate (serial 28:01:5a:de ) was revoked the same hour. A role named agent-endpoint already existed there and was overwritten without being read, so its earlier settings are lost. The csr-signer policy gained pki-agents/sign/agent-endpoint in the same write. Both were removed later that day, when the role was written on pki-agents-v2 . pki-agents-v2 already carried agent-endpoint and agent-client , both allowing agents.weftspun , stonecat-ratio.ts.net and tailnet addresses. The existing agent-endpoint had a one-year ceiling and stored each certificate; this RFD's write changed it to 90 days and no_store . The Mac's own server certificate came from that role before the change. The operator then requested the old settings back. Only the root token can write the role, and it sits in the password manager, which routine work does not use. The operator kept the 90-day role and had both certificates rotated through it instead. The certificates in use Both were rotated on 2026-10-16 with a fresh P-256 key made on each host and signed by the Mac agent identity with no root token. Each is valid to 2027-01-14, passes the chain gate, and matches its key. - fedora-9a6c28.agents.weftspun , serial 5d:9c:e6:f3 , at ~/.bao-creds/fedora-9a6c28/srv-fullchain.pem . It replaces serial 21:f0:0c:1d , issued earlier the same day, never served, and deleted with its key. - mac-mini-fire-01b8f5.agents.weftspun , serial 3e:dd:70:c0 , at ~/.bao-creds/mac-mini-fire-01b8f5/srv-fullchain.pem . It replaces serial 60:1e:4b:98 , a one-year certificate from the old role. No agent identity may revoke on pki-agents-v2 , so that one stays valid to 2027-10-12; nothing on the Mac reads it. Related - RFD66606-2142 (Bao PKI service TLS), the first PKI mount. - RFD66606-2145 (certificate lifetimes), the 90-day leaf ceiling. - RFD66606-2316 (Bao bounded storage), why no record is stored. - RFD66606-2311 (Bonsai 2 serving), the first host to need this. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2319: a serving host's certificate comes from agent CA v2

b: State: committed Feature: an MCP agent session on the Mac launches, sees and drives the OXRSys Simulator through cua-driver, in the background Scope: XR Pilot's oxrsys/docs/xr-cua-oxrsys.md and oxrsys/scripts/xr-cua-oxrsys-register.sh An agent sees and drives the OXRSys Simulator on the Mac without taking the operator's focus. The simulator is a desktop window. Without a way for an agent to see it and give it input, every simulator run needed a person at the keyboard. An agent drives the OXRSys Simulator on the Mac through cua-driver's own MCP server, registered under the name xr-cua-oxrsys . It launches the simulator, reads the decoded preview as pixels and the control row as accessibility elements, and sends keys, clicks, typing and scrolls into the view. Every call runs in the background: no focus change and no cursor move, so the operator keeps working in another window. The operator ruled it done on 2026-10-17. Run scripts/xr-cua-oxrsys-register.sh to register xr-cua-oxrsys ; it prints the diff. Setup cua-driver is installed once on the Mac and reused across projects. Its accessibility and screen-recording grants belong to the driver app, not to the terminal that runs the agent. scripts/xr-cua-oxrsys-register.sh writes the xr-cua-oxrsys entry (command cua-driver , argument mcp ) into the agent's MCP settings, keeps every other server and prints the diff. A running session picks the entry up when it reconnects its MCP servers. Where it landed XR Pilot's repository, commit "Add xr-cua-oxrsys as the automation surface for the simulator" (2026-10-01): the document and the installer, 91 lines in two files. The plan tool landed there in "Add a plan tool that acts out a taskweft RECTGTN task network" (2026-10-04). What it leaves out - The headset side, a second server reached over SSH, is not on main . The document places it on the Flow 2 branch, and docs/platforms/ does not exist on main (read 2026-10-17). - The simulator does not ship with cua-driver. - The name ends in -oxrsys so it does not clash with the headset-side server. Related - RFD66606-2235, the agent that plans with taskweft through the editor, done in desktop mode through XR Pilot's plan tool. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
