b: State: committed Feature: each fighter in the SolidCraft autobattler is a Frame put together from guest solids, rolled on survey tables, and it carries wear from round to round Scope: the SolidCraft autobattler: its game script, its page and its zone version Autobattler fighters are Frames that carry wear from round to round. Each unit was one bare solid with no identity, and every round started from zero. Nothing on screen said which unit was hurt or why a round ended. Each squad in the SolidCraft autobattler fields five Frames. A Frame's body is put together from solids the guest kernel builds, and its species, presentation and age come from three d100 rolls on the population survey tables of our appendix-E dataset. A Frame that survives a round stays with wear and leaves after five rounds, and each side earns scrip per round, as in the Gyre setting. The operator asked for more Frames, game feel, the Gyre flavour and readability on 2026-10-17. Run the game script with --selftest and --rounds=N to read a sim of the rounds. Roles, props and the zone as requested Each Frame also has one of three roles, melee, range or cyber, that beat each other as in rock, paper, scissors. The operator requested the roles on 2026-10-18. Each role and the plant also need a prop in a mirrored arena: cover, a relay per side or soil. The operator requested them the same day. On 2026-10-19 the operator requested that the game also run as a fabric zone that headsets join, with the store kept off every frame and every tick. Sources Drafted on 2026-10-17 from the game script as shipped, its self-test logs on each system and the operator's requests of the same day. What a Frame is The guest builds 18 solids while the game loads: 12 whole solids and six parts (a head, a limb, a torso, a ring, a cube and a base). A Frame places parts by species and merges them into one mesh, so a Frame is one draw call. The parts become separate pieces only when it breaks. The bounds of the parts set health, damage, speed and reach, as the single solid did before. - Species: humanoid 1-50, semi-humanoid 51-88, synthetic 89-94, uplifted animal 95-96, plant 97-98, exotic 99-100. - Presentation: feminine 1-71, masculine 72-89, other 90-100. - Age: youth 1-58, juvenile 59-75, adult 76-87, no age 88-99, infant 100. The bands are the raw survey distribution, tables E.8 to E.10. Age scales the body and the head. Each species but humanoid adds one trait: semi-humanoid is fast, uplifted animal is very fast with less health, synthetic is plated and slower, plant regrows and is slow, and exotic is one bare whole solid that hits hard. Wear and scrip A Frame that survives a round gains one point of wear, and its maximum health drops by a tenth of its base for each point. At five points it leaves. New drafts fill the empty places. Each side earns two scrip per round plus one per Frame left, and the winner three more. Feel and readability A hit flashes the Frame and plays a short generated sound. A Frame that breaks throws its parts and shakes the camera. Each Frame has a health bar and a name tag, a little of its side's colour shows even in shade, and the end of a round shows the Frames left and the scrip earned. Roles Melee beats range, range beats cyber and cyber beats melee. A hit on the role the attacker beats does 1.6 times its damage, a hit on the role that beats it does 0.6 times, and a hit on the same role does its normal damage. Reach puts the roles in order: melee hits at the reach of its body, cyber at 3.8 m and range at 7 m, so a range Frame shoots a cyber Frame before the cyber Frame can answer, and a melee Frame has to close the gap to a range Frame. - Melee: 1.25 times the health, 1.15 times the speed, an attack every 0.8 s, and a shield in front. Its hits push the target back. - Range: 0.75 times the health, 0.8 times the damage, 0.9 times the speed, an attack every 1.1 s, and a barrel at the shoulder. Each shot is a small sphere that flies to the target. - Cyber: 0.95 times the health, 0.7 times the damage, an attack every 1.0 s, and a dish on top. Each hit adds 0.7 s to the target's next attack and shows a ring that spreads over the target. The role's parts come from the same catalog of guest solids and merge into the Frame's one mesh, but they do not count toward its health, damage or reach. Each squad's draft holds every role at least once, so every round shows the triangle. The other two places draw a role at random from the round's seed. The name tag shows the role before the species. What the world gives each role Each role and the plant now need something in the arena, so a sim shows what the world adds and what it takes away. The operator requested these props on 2026-10-18, for every role at once so that no role is the only one that depends on the world. - Range needs a clear line. Five cover blocks stand in the middle. A range Frame does not shoot through cover. It walks around the block until the line is clear. Every Frame walks around cover, not through it. - Cyber needs its relay. Each side has a relay mast, with its reach drawn as a faint disc on the floor. A cyber Frame jams only within 6.5 m of its own standing relay; away from it, the hit does half damage and no jam. A cyber Frame waits at the edge of the disc while friends who are not cyber still fight. Any Frame can attack the enemy relay (160 health). A relay that goes down stays down until the next round. - Melee needs open ground. Within 0.9 m of cover a melee Frame moves at 0.6 times its speed and its hits do not push the target back. - A plant needs soil. It regrows (4 health per second) only on one of four soil patches. Below half health it walks to the nearest patch and stays until it is nearly whole. Equity is a property of the layout: each prop has a twin of the same shape at the mirror place across the middle line, side 0's relay is on side 0's half, and a tie in which way to walk round cover goes the same way for both sides. The self-test checks the mirror and fails when one block is moved 0.5 m (the control). It also checks that a line through the middle block is blocked and a line past the blocks is clear. Each round prints a WORLD line: seconds range Frames spent with no clear line, cyber hits with and without the relay, seconds melee Frames spent beside cover, seconds plants spent on soil, and each relay's health. --rounds=N with --selftest runs N rounds for a longer sim. Zone server and VR mode The round is deterministic: one seed gives the same ROUND , DAMAGE and WORLD lines on the web and on the three desktop systems. That makes the game a fit for an authoritative zone. The zone server runs the round headless, and every client shows the same round. Three loops run at three rates, and only the last touches the store. - The headset renders at 144 Hz, a frame every 6.9 ms. It predicts poses locally and never waits on the network or on a commit. - The zone runs the round at a fixed tick. At the start of a round it sends the seed and both drafts on a reliable stream. Each tick it sends every Frame's place and health as datagrams, where the next tick replaces a lost one, and hits, breaks and the round's end on the reliable stream. The zone and transport are those of interactor-fabric-zone ( 3-interactor/fabric-zone ). - After a tick, the zone hands its SQLite journal image to a save thread if it changed. The save thread writes the image to SQLite on FoundationDB ( datasource-store ( 6-datasource/store )) and keeps only the newest one: a save that is still in flight when the next is ready is replaced, not queued. A slow commit makes the stored image older. It never holds a tick or a frame. The store's place in the third loop comes from a measurement. On 2026-10-19, sixteen players committing one row 20 times a second waited 5.5 to 6.0 ms for the median commit on the Windows desk's FoundationDB under WSL, and over one player-day the worst waits reached 3.3 to 4.7 s. A typical commit is already a whole frame at 144 Hz, and the worst is hundreds of frames. The zone version lives in a new interactor repository, named interactor-solidcraft-zone and placed in the goal manifest when it is made. The game's Godot project moves there as the one source, with a zone-server mode and a headset mode. The Space keeps the web build and the downloads, built from that repository. The guest kernel and the zone repository stay as they are and are used as dependencies. Each step has a check, and each check has a control. - The Space's web build prints the same lines after the move as before it. - Two headless clients beside a zone server print the server's ROUND , DAMAGE and WORLD lines. A client given another seed must differ. - The headset mode runs under the XR Pilot desktop runtime, which an agent drives with no person in a headset. - The save thread reports the age of the newest stored image over a player-day: its worst and how often it passes 1, 2 and 5 s. The planted slow commit must raise it. The zone simulates at 60 Hz and sends rows under RFD66606-2326's byte budget. Two choices are open: whether the headset client is the V-Sekai client or a scene in the game's own project, and which host runs FoundationDB in production. A run on a plain Linux runner, pending on 2026-10-19, says whether the multi-second waits come from the WSL host. The autobattler is the network test bench RFD66606-2326's numbers so far come from walkers generated for the test, whose rows never repeat. The autobattler gives real traffic with an answer key. One seed fixes every round, so the server's replay of a seed is the truth for every row a client receives, at every tick. - Scale. One zone runs many arenas side by side, from one to a few hundred, each a round of ten Frames on its own seed, with headless players placed so their view holds from tens to thousands of Frames. Arenas start a few ticks apart, so hits, breaks and round ends spread over time. - Classes. The zone carries what the game carries, not one kind of mover: Frames on scripted moves, players' tracked heads and hands, props at rest that change only when touched, and crowds of pedestrians who stop, start and walk in pairs. Headless players replay recorded head and hand tracks, since tracked motion has sensor jitter a script lacks. Every report is split by class. - Scenes. Crowds come as the scenes people make: a shopping street, a standing concert, a seated stadium with a wave, a queue, a scramble crossing, a dance floor, a parade, a festival plaza, a theatre, a picnic lawn, an exit through one door, and a ring of players talking. Each scene's density and pace come from footage counted the way the blue-hour street walk was, and in social scenes most of the crowd is tracked players. - Oracle. Each headless client decodes its rows, moves Frames along their sent velocity between rows, and compares what it holds with the server's replay of the same seeds. It reports the worst position error and how long a Frame stayed wrong. A client must never hold a Frame the replay says has left, or a value that was never sent. - Link. Between server and clients sits a relay that drops and delays datagrams: no loss, 1% and 5%, at 50, 100 and 200 ms of round trip. - Record. The relay writes every message it passes. The recordings are the corpus for the static zstd dictionary: dictionaries built from them at 1, 8, 64, 256 and 1024 MB are measured on held-out recordings in bytes per row, and the size stops growing where the gain flattens. - Report. Bytes per player per second against the budget, bytes per row for plain zstd, for patch-from against the last row the client acknowledged, and for each dictionary size, and the oracle's errors. Saves go through the store's latest-wins thread and report save age. On rows generated for the test, sent as the gap from the client's own prediction, props at rest cost 0.31 bytes a row, pedestrians 2.16 and tracked points 3.96. Walkers that never stop cost 0.47, which flatters prediction, so the bench uses pedestrians and never zombies. Scripted scenes flatter it the same way: a scripted queue, wave or crossing cost 0.31 to 0.34, the price of a prop at rest, and a scripted concert 2.04. Scenes are replayed from recorded motion where a licence allows, and a scene full of players costs what their tracked heads and hands cost. The budget gives players near each other the first share, and the bench sets the split from recorded traffic. Each measurement has a planted defect that must show in the report: - the budget ignored, which must push bytes per second over it; - a client holding another dictionary version, which must fail to decode and never decode wrong values; - the clock counter per row, which must make a client order rows wrong past 256 rows in a tick; - the velocity scale read per tick, which must raise position error; - a dropped leave message, which must leave a Frame the replay has removed; - the store's slow commit, which must raise save age and nothing else. What was measured The change is in the game script only, so the guest and every translation hash stayed valid. On 2026-10-17 the web build and the macOS, Windows and Linux zips each started translated, built 18 solids and printed RESULT PASS . The script cost per physics frame rose from about 0.23 ms to about 0.3 ms on the Mac. The web game's slowest frame in the first round read 139 to 145 ms before and after. Native frame times on the Mac were not compared: other jobs on the same machine made them vary more than the change. On 2026-10-18 the roles changed the game script only, again. The self-test first checks the triangle: every role beats exactly one other and loses to exactly one. A control table in which melee loses to both others must fail the same check, and it does. The macOS, Windows and Linux zips and the web build in a desktop browser then printed the same two rounds, with the same winners and the same damage per pair of roles, and RESULT PASS . In round 1, range did 303 damage to cyber and cyber did 57 to range. The web game's slowest frame in round 1 read 150 ms with the roles and 134 ms without them, one run each in the same browser, so the difference is not measured past noise. The release kept its tag, because the guest did not change. Its zips and SHA256SUMS were replaced. On 2026-10-18 the world props changed the game script only, a third time. The self-test printed WORLD mirror=true control=false line_through=false line_beside=true on each system. The macOS, Windows and Linux zips and the web build in a desktop browser printed the same ROUND , DAMAGE and WORLD lines for the four rounds they share. The web run went on to nine rounds and the macOS run to twelve. Over the twelve rounds each side won six. Per round, range Frames spent 0.3 to 3.0 s with no clear line, melee Frames spent 1.2 to 9.0 s beside cover, and cyber Frames landed 1 to 17 hits with the relay and 0 to 13 without it. Plants stood on soil in four of the twelve rounds, for up to 8.0 s. Plants are 2 in 100 of the species rolls, so a sim that wants to read the soil rule needs many rounds. No relay went down in the twelve rounds (the lowest read 103 of 160). The first version moved a blocked range Frame sideways only, and in one round two range Frames stayed blocked for 34 s until the 45 s limit ended it. A blocked range Frame now walks around the block, and no round of the twelve reached the limit. The problem Each unit was one solid: a box, a cylinder, a sphere or a torus. Related - RFD66606-2379, where the desktop builds ship: the release that carries this game. - RFD66606-2085, RFD66606-2091 and RFD66606-2120, the Gyre setting (abandoned): the source of Frames, wear and scrip. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2321: the autobattler fields Frames that wear

b: State: discussion Feature: the pen's MESH stage moves a garment that clips the body out of it Scope: the fit in the drape guest, its kernels, and the pen's MESH stage Can the pen's skirt leave the body without a wider clearance on the strokes? On the statue avatar's body, the scripted skirt's surface sits 12 to 17 mm inside the cone its rings are sized for, about an AA battery's width, between the front and back seams. - MESH ends with a fit. A garment surface that clips the body is moved out of it by the fit, not by a wider clearance on the strokes (operator, 2026-10-27). - The fit follows the intersection-free retargeting fork's start: the body begins shrunk along its vertex normals, so the drawn surface is outside it, and grows back to full size in steps. - Each step is one solve by contract-lbfgsb ( 2-contract/lbfgsb ) on the GPU: the shape term keeps the drawn surface's shape, and the IPC barrier keeps every vertex outside the body at that step's size. Every iterate stays intersection-free. - The fit runs in the guest of interactor-drape ( 3-interactor/drape ), which already drives the solver on RenderingDevice and holds the IPC kernels. drape.elf comes back to transport-meshing-pen ( 1-transport/meshing-pen ) (operator, 2026-10-27). - The pen's check that no garment vertex is inside the body reads the fitted mesh. The scripted skirt's ring clearance goes back to 1 cm, a little more than a pencil's width. Read the gates and controls below, then run the pen's check that no garment vertex is inside the body on the fitted skirt. The problem Nine of 1910 vertices end up 3 to 12 mm inside the body, from two pennies to nearly a AA battery's width. A 2 cm ring clearance, two AAA batteries side by side, hides it without moving the surface. The solve For grow fraction a from 0 to 1 in N steps, the body is B(a) = B − (1 − a) d0 n , with n the area-weighted vertex normals of the body and d0 the shrink depth. At each step the solver minimises over the garment vertices x : E(x) = ks sum over edges ( xi − xj − lij)^2 + kl sum over vertices L x − L x0 ^2 + kappa sum over vertices, candidate triangles of B(a): b(d^2) lij and L x0 are the drawn surface's edge lengths and Laplacian coordinates, and b is the IPC log barrier of the drape kernel, zero beyond dhat . The step starts from the last step's result. What exists, and what is new - L-BFGS-B on the GPU: contract-lbfgsb vec_rd , in the drape guest, run by its solver tests. - IPC point-triangle barrier: drape IpcPointTriangle.lean , gradient and Hessian, no energy. - IPC step bound: drape IpcStepClamp.lean , written, not emitted or wired. - Shape term and normal shrink: new. - Fit entry points in the guest: new. New in the kernels: - The barrier's energy, summed per vertex, because a line search compares energies. - The step bound inside the line search: the solver's largest step is capped so no vertex moves more than a fraction of its distance to the body. Candidate triangles for each vertex come from the body mesh on the guest's CPU, once per step. Gates and controls - No vertex inside: 0 inside, by winding number, after the fit. Control that must fail: the fit off, where the statue skirt has 9 inside. - Every iterate outside: 0 inside after every step. Control: the step bound off. - The start: 0 inside against the shrunk body. Control: d0 = 0 on the statue skirt. - The shape kept: the move of each vertex is reported. No control, because it is a measurement. Each runs on the scripted skirt (two avatars), the replayed skirt and dress, and the two hand-drawn skirts. The fit runs on RenderingDevice only. The solver's vector ops keep their CPU-against-GPU unit tests. What is not known - ks , kl , kappa , dhat , d0 and N : measured on the fixtures first. - Time per fit on the GPU for about 2000 garment vertices. - Whether float32 vectors converge with the barrier near a 1 mm dhat , about a card's thickness. - The statue's body is open (870 boundary edges, 28 components): whether its normals give a clean shrink. Related - RFD66606-2293, which cut the fit from the pen; RFD66606-2294, where compute runs. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2337: a garment fit at MESH on the GPU L-BFGS-B

b: State: discussion Feature: a persona answers from a goal-task network instead of from weights Scope: the persona repository, the planner it requires as a library, and its register row A persona answers from a goal-task network, so a goal gives an exact plan with no sampling. A request in words reaches a persona only by way of whoever authors the domain. A domain with a thin vocabulary answers a thin set of goals. - A persona answers from a goal-task network rather than from weights: a domain and a goal go in, an exact plan comes out, and no sampling is involved (operator, 2026-10-30). - The persona is the instinct model: Lean 4 code, named for its latency against a language model (operator, 2026-10-29). - The planner is a library, not a reference. The persona requires the RECTGTN domain over GitHub, as the character domain does, and composes in its shared GTN space. - Its inputs are a code or a number. A code is the vocabulary: one level count a dimension, packed mixed-radix, the shape residual FSQ stacks its stages in. - A code the codebook does not hold, a variable the domain does not declare, and a goal the domain cannot reach are refused by name. Read RFD66606-2292 next, the organization domain this workspace's RFDs render into. Where it lives It is its own repository on the interactor side, placed when it is created, and the planner revision it builds against is recorded in its manifest. What landed The persona is a Lean package of its own: a domain of state variables, a codebook and actions, a goal over the planner's own node space, and a search that composes the plan. The landing subject is "Compose the persona in Lean over the planner library". Its gate is a witness exe with a positive and a negative control per invariant: the codebook's size, basis and mixed-radix index; a code past its level and a code of the wrong arity both refused; a plan that executes to the goal; and three refusals, an unreachable goal, an undeclared variable and zero fuel. The codebook is the vocabulary Eight levels over four dimensions is 4096 codes a stage, and four stages of those is 281474976710656 codes from thirty-two small integers. A code is what a goal argument binds, and a number is the other half of the surface. The codec is the one this workspace already certifies for the residual-FSQ recommender: a mixed-radix index over per-dimension levels, injective and bounded at the real scale. References The codebook's shape and the stages it stacks come from this lineage. - Zeghidour et al., SoundStream (doi 10.1109/TASLP.2021.3130651) - Défossez et al., EnCodec (doi 10.48550/arXiv.2210.13438) - Mentzer et al., Finite Scalar Quantization (doi 10.48550/arXiv.2309.15505) - Zhu et al., Robust Residual FSQ (doi 10.48550/arXiv.2508.15860) - Liu et al., VQTalker (doi 10.48550/arXiv.2412.09892) The design's other half The persona is the half that answers from a program. The other half is a language model, and the design keeps a place for it until the model has a home (operator, 2026-10-29). Code as data, and what a persona says back A caller gives category and numeric instructions, and the persona walks the programs it holds: "you did not even weight paint", then what face tracking costs. The caller is given options, and a choice fits the input shape rather than arriving in words. A failure and a success each point at a guide, baked in or linked (operator, 2026-10-29). What is not known - How a persona composes with this workspace's rendered problems, which the organization domain answers today through the planner's Elixir consumer. - The temporal reading of a domain that declares no reads and no writes: the plan order is exact, and the timeline parallelizes what the domain leaves undeclared. The problem A persona cannot answer a question that is not a goal. The tuples rebac rfd-2339--provides--persona-goal-task-planner rfd-2339--is-a--model-pipeline-stage Related - RFD66606-2292, the organization domain this workspace's own RFDs render into. - RFD66606-2232, the renderer that turns an RFD into a planning problem. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.
t: RFD66606-2339: a persona answers from a planning domain

b: State: discussion Feature: the parked work that no numbered dev rung has claimed Scope: everything past dev.2 that waits for a rung of its own Parked work waits in one place, and no open rung changes to make room for it. Reducing churn is an absolute requirement. An ask added to an open rung moves its pins or edits its file, which the churn gate counts as a failure. dev.next holds every ask that no numbered rung has claimed. An idea that arrives while a rung is open is written here, and the open rung's definition does not change. An item leaves dev.next when a numbered rung is planned around it. Write a new ask into dev.next instead of an open rung, and check that the open rung's file and pins stay unchanged. The sections below list the parked items. The parked items - An original mascot, swapped into the stand-in mascot's three slots (the tray icon, the popup, the requests in the world). - A thematic world that replaces the placeholder backstory and explains the dummy, the requests, the shared world and the persistence. - The vehicle story, chosen as a ladder of choices. You carry the atelier as a sample case and deploy it on any flat surface. The dress form is in the lid and the ledger is the lining. Closing the case writes the journal. Opening it replays the journal. AR comes first: the alpha blend mode with nothing drawn behind the case, which OXRSys already accepts with passthrough_enabled . VR is the same scene in the opaque mode. The case is the town (operator, 2026-10-09): opened, it holds the procedural station town the pen already vendors (MIT) as a diorama you look into, like a tabletop Japanese town built in a wooden tray. It is not a case of building pieces carried through a full-size town. This is the station RFD66606-2343 left for a later rung. The surface is found by MoGe-3 (MIT) when you set the case down. In AR it reads the colour stereo pair from the headset's colour camera module, on the expansion port. The built-in cameras are monochrome and are not used. In a social VR world we did not build, it reads the rendered eye pair. Its metric points and normals give the plane, and the second eye checks the first. Without root, the headset's runtime publishes one colour view as a loopback camera that the video group can read. It advertises 1920x1080 at 30 fps and measured 1.4 to 3.8 fps. Its own camera API is off by default. MoGe-3 runs as a godot-sandbox guest ELF on ggml-rd, the shape RFD66606-2272 proved for segmentation. Its weights come through the weight pump, and no Python is in the running path. It spends no innovation token: it is one more guest on the route zone.elf and curvenet.elf already use. With no confident plane, the case falls back to the controller pose. Its dense graph is 1,406 nodes. ggml-rd lacks only replicate padding and one antialiased resize. Its sparse 3D refiner has no ggml-rd kernels and is left out. Passthrough is tested sim-to-real in virtual worlds only. Two held-out sets are frozen before they render: path-traced rooms built from CC0 scanned furniture, and the station, whose build publishes every seat height. The station set matters because MoGe is unproven on stylized frames. Gate: the surface under the crosshair, scaled by the floor at the tracked eye height, lies within 3 cm of truth. Controls: a frame with no flat surface must fall back, and GGML_RD_FAULT=1 must fail the fit. RFD66606-2313 parks the full loop over colour passthrough on this surface. - Lookdev: style frames for the world, the mascot, Maro in SCSS and the dummy. Image generation waits for a rung. - A mechanics search, ranked by best-of-breed sorting and valuation. A first pass on public evidence is running, and its result lands here. - Shared-world building gameplay, which follows from the world and the mechanics search. - The shared world of two, cut from the first dev.2 draft (operator, 2026-10-12): the tray as zone host for two clients over ENet on localhost, the FDB-SQLite wardrobe that survives a zone restart, the three fabric-zone changes ( set_payload and zone_despawn , Journal::replay on open, the payload in pack_intent ), the stand-in mascot's 36 never-repeating requests with one constraint each, the backstory, the fourteen signs and the ledger board, two procedural audio cues, and the two-person playtest. - Wearing on Maro: the fit against her body mesh, the clothing hide in the same frame, no bone off rest scale, the pop-on, and Maro in the ported SCSS. No dev.2 gate reaches past MESH. - The avatar's tail opening (operator, 2026-10-17). The opening is cut in the cardigan, the outer layer, fitted tight around the tail's base, and the dress keeps a small slot under it. No flap, lap panel, ruffle trim or bow covers it, and the tail is kept. The cut is the tail base's sweep over the motion clips plus 5 mm. The tail's long strands still cross the cardigan in motion. That is open. - The Windows x86_64 executable, signing once a legal entity is chosen, spatial voice, controller walking and the first headset test. - The guest transport (QUIC, TLS and the session CA in guests) for friends over the internet. - The Hilbert AOI band ported into zone.elf , for neighbour zones. - Binary translation in the pen (dev.3 logbook). The pen's tools/build.exs sets GODOT_SANDBOX_BINTR_UNITS , compiles the units in parallel and links one library per guest, and the pen vendors an addon at or after the godot-sandbox commit the dev.3 logbook names. Split into 24 units, usd compiled and linked in 81 s; as one file it ran past 7 min on one core. Gate: every guest the probe loads reports translated. Control: the probe with no bintr/ fails by name. - The dev.3 gaps, each counted in the dev.3 logbook: the CASSIE dress replay (90 of 102 cycles) and a dress-layer control; the OpenXR alert that hangs a gate with no runtime; --xr-mode off in the world-grab usage line; a stall control in the pen's reliability gate; a churn tool with its planted pin bump; a windowed Windows export in the tray's release.exs ; the tray's Dock tile. - RFD66606-2349's file check on the house recorder's recordings, which dev.3 did not run (dev.3 logbook, The verdict). The recorder's MKV carries CineForm frames, the codec a .cfhd holds. av1mkv builds on Windows only; the MKV reader in entities-godot's media I/O can read it on any desk (operator, 2026-10-12). - A pin for every project a rung names, as a commit or as a tag-like branch that does not move by convention (operator, 2026-10-20: branches are preferred). The private manifest tracked 8 of its projects at main , the tray and the double engine among them, so a merge moved what a sync checks out and the churn gate counted nothing (dev.3 logbook, gate 8). tools/churn_gate.exs now reads a branch row's tip from the checkout, now and at open, and a moved tip fails by name, so main cannot serve as a rung's pin. - A loading screen in the pen (operator, 2026-10-12): the app shows it from launch until the world is ready, in place of the engine's boot splash, which every dev.3 recording opens on for up to 30 s. It is not white or drab (operator, 2026-10-12): it carries the world's own colour and something that moves, so a wait reads as the app. The pen is an upstream fork read-only from the private org, so it lands through the pen's own repo and a pin bump. - No magenta in the pen (operator, 2026-10-12: "magenta is ugly"). The dev.3 recordings in flat mode (the orbit, gate 1 flat and the drop_seam control) show the engine's missing-texture magenta, so a material does not load there. A gate check fails a frame that carries it, with a planted missing texture as the control. - Gate recordings from the runtime's stream, not the screen (dev.3 logbook, Recordings): four of eight screen captures miss the gate's subject. With it, an orbit that drives the camera the window draws from, so the contact sheet shows ten views. - A fast loop split from the soak (operator, 2026-10-12). Every gate's quick form runs on each change, about 2 min in all. The 30-minute soaks run once per rung, in the background, and never hold the logbook or the pull request; their result is appended when it lands. dev.3 spent about 70 min of its cycle on soaks run one after another. - Three tray checks that dev.3 left NOT RUN (operator, 2026-10-12): the first launch past the OS download warning, which needs a download that carries the mark of the web and a person to click Run anyway, and the install from a fresh account, on Windows and on macOS. - decider-pong, a Pong recording where a live model drives one paddle. It sits in the interactor tier, beside its pinned upstream decider. Two questions wait for a rung. Its Python breaks the languages rule, so it is ported to Elixir or to the engine, or it gets a named exemption. Its name lacks the interactor side prefix, which needs a rename by the user on the forge and one manifest line. RFD66606-2346 records how it was placed. Parked work held in manifest issues Each item below has an issue on the private manifest, which holds the state and how to resume. - One set of repository settings across the two orgs, the pr-credit lease, and the private bootstrap's Nushell, Erlang and Elixir tools. - The Lean v4.34.1 move, 43 of 45 pull requests merged, and the CI circuit breaker. - The Sakuragaoka Station port: the blossom cluster LOD, the headset budget and the credit ledger. - XR Pilot fixes, one CI slot per repository, and the org's CI state. - An honest real-time Snake video, recorded with the house recorder in CineForm. - The forge READMEs still off the house shape, and the README churn gate run on this workspace. The problem Parked work still needs one place to wait. Related - RFD66606-2342, dev.1; RFD66606-2343, dev.2; RFD66606-2344, dev.3. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.

b: State: committed Feature: a tray icon with the stand-in mascot's face on macOS and Windows, the first dev rung Scope: the tray's v -dev.1 release The tray icon ships first: one Godot scene with a borrowed mascot's face. Install, integrity, silence and uninstall must work before anything is drawn. dev.1 ships one Godot scene, built with the pinned double editor and exported with its templates for macOS and Windows. A borrowed mascot's face is the icon. A click opens a popup with the version, a headset line, a zone line, a disabled "Draw" button and the mascot playing Idle. Run the gates in tools/gate_dev1.exs against OXRSys. dev.1: the feature One Godot scene, built with the pinned double editor and exported with its templates for macOS and Windows. The stand-in mascot's face is the icon. Clicking it opens a popup with: - the version; - a "headset: connected / not found" line; - a "zone: none" line; - a disabled "Draw" button; - a viewport where the mascot's glb plays Idle with its own materials. The tray becomes the zone host and the desktop client's launcher in dev.2, so it comes first. - macOS: a menu-bar status item via DisplayServer.create_status_indicator , guarded by has_feature(FEATURE_STATUS_INDICATOR) ; ad-hoc signed; a DMG. - Windows: a system tray icon via the same API; a zip. The mascot is borrowed third-party work under MIT, not ours. It is the stand-in for dev.1 and dev.2, and no public asset shows it. The pins, frozen from open to tag This file names every pin when the rung opens, and nothing moves until the rung tags. Bumps happen between rungs, as one batch, recorded in the logbook. - Engine: our Godot build fork's release v20260930-double.1, at the engine ref its release notes name, with the macOS arm64 editor and templates and the Windows x86_64 templates. - OXRSys and xr_pilot_mcp : our XR pilot interactor at the commit the logbook names. - The headset probe: the pen's OpenXR probe, from our meshing pen at the commit the logbook names. - The mascot: the borrowed stand-in (MIT), from the private character repo. The reliability gate Every client logs frame times. At most 1 frame in 100,000 may exceed twice its budget (27.8 ms at 72 Hz), with zero crashes and zero disconnects across the playtest. It is measured on OXRSys and on the flat client. Control: a planted 30 ms stall every 10,000 frames must fail by count. Gates and controls The tray's tools/gate_dev1.exs runs these against OXRSys. 1. Install and launch from a fresh user account. The icon appears within 5 s. The version matches the tag. Control: a wrong version string must fail by name. 2. Integrity. Signing waits on a signing identity, so dev.1 ships ad-hoc signed on macOS and unsigned on Windows, with one documented first-launch override. A SHA-256 per artifact is published and checked. Control: a tampered artifact must fail its hash by name. 3. "headset: connected" only when an OpenXR session can be created on OXRSys. Control: XR_RUNTIME_JSON at a missing file must give "not found". 4. Zero outbound connections in a 10-minute idle capture. Control: the off-by-default update check, switched on, must show exactly one. 5. Uninstall leaves nothing behind. Control: a planted stray file must be named. 6. The mascot's Idle plays in the popup, and the reliability gate holds over a 30-minute idle run. Controls: the glb removed must fail by path; the planted stall must fail by count. 7. Churn: zero pin moves and zero edits to this RFD between open and tag. Control: a planted pin bump must fail by name. The playtest The user, a teammate and one trusted outsider each install on a Mac or PC they own, from the release page, with no help beyond the written first-launch override. Pass: three icons running at day's end. Every install question is logged. b: State: committed Feature: one intermediate format for every rendered video Scope: every tool in the workspace that writes a video file, first the decider-pong interactor Every rendered video is one format: CineForm and FLAC in Matroska. The decider-pong recorders wrote H.264 and AAC in MP4. That is a lossy delivery format, and a second encode loses more. Every rendered video is written as CineForm video and FLAC audio in a Matroska ( .mkv ) file. CineForm runs at gbrp12le , so RGB frames keep full chroma. MP4 is blocklisted as a container, and H.264 and AAC are not written as outputs. A tool that writes video refuses an output path that does not end in .mkv . Uncompressed PCM audio is accepted in place of FLAC (operator, 2026-10-23); both are lossless. Check a video with ffprobe , which must report cfhd , gbrp12le , 1920x1080 and the matroska format. Also related - The private blocklist, which lists MP4. - The decider-pong skill carries the same rule for agents. Why an intermediate An intermediate must survive re-encoding and keep sharp synthetic edges. Encoder settings The homebrew ffmpeg ships the cfhd encoder. It takes yuv422p10le , gbrp12le and gbrap12le . The recorders use gbrp12le , because their frames are RGB and Pong's edges are one colour against another. Audio is FLAC, or uncompressed PCM, at 48 kHz, stereo. An engine movie writer receives 32-bit samples, so it writes pcm_s24le and never 16-bit. CineForm fails on a frame whose width is not divisible by 16 or whose height is not divisible by 8. A writer checks the size before it starts and refuses with a message that names the size, because the encoder otherwise dies mid-stream and the only symptom is a broken pipe. A live recorder pipes raw RGB to one ffmpeg process that writes CineForm in Matroska, then a second pass copies that video and adds the FLAC track. Nothing is held in memory past the pipe. Cost On the Mac mini, cfhd encodes a 1080p test source at about 170 frames a second, so a 30 fps live render keeps up with room to spare. A file grows by about 20 MB a second at 1080p. A 2-minute render is about 2.4 GB and a 5-minute render about 6 GB. The Desktop filled to 43 GB in one session, so superseded renders are listed for deletion and deleted only on request. How a file is checked ffprobe must report cfhd , gbrp12le , 1920x1080, flac or a pcm_s16le / pcm_s24le stream at 48000 Hz and the matroska format, with the duration the run asked for. A frame is then pulled with ffmpeg -ss and looked at. That report and that frame are the check, whatever exit code the recorder returns. The guard and its control recorder_second_opinion.py exits with an error on any --out that does not end in .mkv . The planted control asked for planted.mp4 : the run exited 1 and wrote no file. What changed in decider-pong recorder_pong_v.py and recorder_second_opinion.py now write CineForm and FLAC. Four superseded recorders that only wrote MP4 were deleted: recorder_live.py , recorder_pong_live.py , recorder_pong_vector.py and recorder_realtime.py . Every MP4 the session had made was removed and re-rendered. The problem The workspace had no written format, so each recorder picked its own. Related - RFD66606-2349, which replaces the encoder, the live recorder and the file check below. The format here stands. - RFD66606-2346, decider-pong in the workspace; RFD66606-2347, the decider-pong review. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.

b: State: committed Feature: a Pong recording whose labels match what the live model does, and a run where it wins Scope: the decider-pong interactor's recorder_second_opinion.py , its simulators, evals and PEER_REVIEW.md A live Pong model wins 7-0 and 8-0, and the write-up says who does the predicting. The shipped video showed "a live decider" playing Pong. The model was right on 34 to 52 percent of its replies, answered "up" most of the time, and lost 0-25 in 2 minutes. The live paddle plays with four parts. Code predicts the y where the ball will reach the paddle by running Pong.step forward. The model answers the sign of the 10-px steps to that point. A held move stops at the target. An answer older than 15 frames hands the paddle to the teacher. With the classic angle rule on both paddles, the model wins 7-0 and 8-0 on its own points over two 5-minute runs. The teacher controls on the same seeds end 7-6 and 9-8. Read PEER_REVIEW.md in decider-pong, which carries every number. The review, in short The shipped prompt scored 68 percent offline, with 41 of 60 answers "up". A held answer overshot: one "move" carries the paddle 40 px over a 4-frame reply, against a 14-px reach. One failed request froze the paddle on "stay" for the rest of a run. The drawn paddles were twice the size of the colliding ones, and the right one sat 10 px behind its hit plane. The overlap test had a wrong y term, the timecode printed hundredths, serves were seeded from the clock, and 600 frames sat in memory. The README contradicted the files on disk. Why the game could not be won Under the repo physics no paddle can win: the teacher never misses. A hit never changes the ball's vertical speed, which stays under 4.1 px a frame. A paddle moves 10 px a frame. Teacher against teacher held 0-0 for 30 simulated minutes on three seeds. The classic angle rule, --english 8 , lets the hit point change the vertical speed by up to 8 px a frame. It applies to both paddles, and teacher against teacher stays even under it. What each step fixed 1. Simulation first. sim_right_paddle.py showed that even a paddle that is always right loses about 4 points a minute when it holds an answer for a 4-frame delay. Aiming at the crossing point and stopping there loses almost none, even with 60 percent wrong answers. 2. Prompt. A two-number prompt at temperature 0 was right 98 percent of the time on spread cases, but 81 percent on gaps under 30 px, where it answered "stay". The STEPS prompt was right on 80 of 80 close calls at a median of about 105 ms. 3. Prediction. A mirror-reflection formula tied 2-2. It was wrong on 80 of 80 approaches, because the game pins the ball to the wall. The rollout matched the real hit-test y on 80 of 80. 4. Staleness. The first 5-minute rollout run led 4-0, then an endpoint stall froze the paddle for about 30 s and it lost 13 points. A 1 s request timeout and a 15-frame answer limit fixed it. A planted endpoint that never answers gave 600 of 600 teacher frames, with the paddle still moving. Results that count Seed 7, 5 minutes: 0-7, all 7 points the model's, 3232 of 3232 replies correct, p50 84 ms. Seed 11, 5 minutes: 2-8. The model's points are 8-0, and the 2 lost came while the teacher held the paddle during 13 endpoint failures. Without the angle rule the rollout run holds 0-0, the most the physics allows. What the win does not show The model answers the sign of a small integer. A rule in code would do the same. It does not plan, aim or read the game. The next test gives the model the game state and scores the target it chooses. Files Every render is CineForm and FLAC in Matroska on the Desktop, named by mode, seed and length, with its decision log. Runs that exposed a bug keep a suffix that says so, such as _stale-reply-bug . The commits that carry this work are on decider-pong main . The problem Code does the predicting in the winning runs, and the write-up must say so. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped.

b: State: committed Feature: one way to record a run where a live model plays Scope: every recording of a live run in the workspace, first the decider games A live run is recorded at 4K, in CineForm, with the house recorder. Movie Maker renders at a fixed frame rate, so the game waits for the model and the video hides its latency. A video of a live model must show the latency it has. A live run is recorded with the house recorder on the Mac at a 3840x2160 canvas. The recorder writes CineForm video and FLAC audio in Matroska through its custom output. The game runs on the wall clock and never waits for the model. Godot Movie Maker is blocklisted. FFmpeg never runs as a tool. RFD66606-2345's format stands; this RFD replaces its encoder, its live recorder and its file check. Read RFD66606-2345 for the format this RFD amends. The operator's rulings, 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10 - The recorder is the house recorder. Movie Maker is blocklisted. - The video is 3840x2160. 2K is denied. - A video holds at least 2 minutes of real run time. A short run is made longer by running longer, never by holding or repeating frames. - The game ticks on the wall clock. A late reply applies at the next tick. With no reply the game takes its default move. - CineForm everywhere. No ProRes is written and converted to CineForm. - FFmpeg never runs as a tool, and headless Godot never runs. How the house recorder writes CineForm The house recorder's current release ships the cfhd CineForm encoder. Its custom output, built on FFmpeg, is set to Matroska with cfhd video and FLAC audio. In a still-frame test every frame decoded through the CineForm SDK at 39.4 dB against the input. The control, the same input shifted 40 px, scored 16.3 dB. Encoding outside the house recorder A render that is not a live capture encodes with the CineForm SDK through the engine's CineForm module or the CineForm interactor. Delivery uses the AV1-in-Matroska interactor's deliver.exs . It rewraps the frames byte for byte and checks every frame and sample. - A render reel records through the engine's movie writer straight to CineForm. It writes no PNG frames to encode later (operator, 2026-10-17). - Large media and videos are kept on the Windows desk, not on the Mac mini, which sits on a remote network (operator, 2026-10-17). A render made on the Mac is copied to the desk, its size is read back there, and only then is the Mac copy deleted. How a file is checked deliver.exs checks every frame and every sample. av1mkv dump-frame pulls frames, and a person looks at them. The run's length is gated from the frames' own timestamps, and a short frame set is the control that must fail. The frames and samples are the check, whatever exit code the recorder returns. Still open - The house recorder's custom output uses FFmpeg's encoder inside the recorder. The ruling bans FFmpeg as a tool, and the Snake video issue records the house recorder as the route. The operator has not ruled on whether the licence reason reaches the house recorder. - The decider-pong recorders named in RFD66606-2345 still call ffmpeg . They move to the house recorder or the SDK route when that project is next worked on. The problem RFD66606-2345 encodes with the homebrew ffmpeg and checks files with ffprobe . FFmpeg as a tool is now banned. b: State: discussion Feature: a token is what the stack cannot run without: twenty, six INNOVATION-TOKENs and fourteen BORING-TOKENs Scope: the token ledger in the private working agreements and the private plan, the private blocklist, and the repos of V-Sekai-fire, chibifire-stages and the private org Which of the twenty tokens are INNOVATION-TOKENs, and which are BORING-TOKENs? The stack crashes without any of the twenty, and only six of them are new risk. A token is a substrate: delete it and the tech stack crashes. The name keeps it apart from a credential (operator, 2026-11-01). The ledger has twenty tokens. Each is a BORING-TOKEN, whose failures are widely known and which runs as shipped, or an INNOVATION-TOKEN, which is our own build, a fork or a use nobody has run. The INNOVATION-TOKENs are guest ELFs on the pinned double engine as row 1, which also runs the pen, zone.elf , the ggml-rd models, slug.elf , voice, the USD guest and the Lean tests, then SQLite on FoundationDB pages as row 2, FEX as row 6, the Fedora cross-build image as row 12, osxcross as row 15 and the taskweft persona engine as row 18. The BORING-TOKENs are Bao as row 3, our fork with an FDB storage backend, then Fly as row 4, which hosts the store, Bao and the KMS key that unseals Bao, then Tailscale as row 5, Proton as row 7, Windows as row 8, pixi as row 9, prek as row 10, GitHub as row 11, LLVM as row 13, llvm-mingw as row 14, SteamVR as row 16, Godot Engine as row 17, Elixir as row 19 and steamac as row 20. The operator ruled Elixir and Proton BORING-TOKENs on 2026-11-01, and Bao a BORING-TOKEN on 2026-11-12 although it is a fork. CockroachDB is retired (operator, 2026-10-18), and the guest BEAM is unship (operator, 2026-10-29). The count was three, then two INNOVATION-TOKENs, and is twenty tokens of which six are INNOVATION-TOKENs. The ledger changes between rungs, not in an open one, and the operator moved the two documents on 2026-10-30 rather than wait for a rung to claim them. Check a new technology against the rule: a token is a substrate, and the tech stack crashes without it. Write it BORING-TOKEN if its failures are widely known, INNOVATION-TOKEN if not. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped. The measured gap The upstream orgs ran a second database. Of 312 repos that use a non-boring technology, 182 fit inside one INNOVATION-TOKEN when each technology is its own. How the ledger was found The operator requested it on 2026-10-18: study the three orgs and consolidate the INNOVATION-TOKENS with frontier learning, with no limit on the count. Each org is a level. Each repo that uses a non-boring technology is a problem: 298 in V-Sekai-fire, 10 in the private org (the local checkouts, because the token cannot list the org) and 4 in chibifire-stages. A problem passes when every technology it uses is in one INNOVATION-TOKEN. Repos were tagged against 33 technologies from their names, descriptions, topics and languages. A step tries one move, "technology X rides on INNOVATION-TOKEN Y". The level with the most regret picks it. The move is kept only when total passes rise and at least two repos use both. Two planted moves with no relation (Ink onto OpenBao, Janet onto CockroachDB) were controls, and both were rejected. What it measured - Passes rose from 182 to 263 of 312 (58% to 84%): 23 moves kept, 11 rejected. - Per level at the end: V-Sekai-fire 251 of 298, the private org 8 of 10, chibifire-stages 4 of 4. - Kept onto the guest INNOVATION-TOKEN: the pen, zone.elf , ggml-rd (and the Python reference models and Slang kernels behind it), MuJoCo, OpenUSD, voice, Rust guests, slug.elf , the double engine with xr-pilot and CineForm, and Lean as tests. - Kept onto the BEAM: taskweft, MCP, holographic reduced representations. - Not merged, for want of shared repos: CockroachDB, the casync chunk store, OpenBao and parquet into the store. Retiring CockroachDB was an operator decision, not a measured one. What is still split - Elixir and guest code meet in 29 repos (taskweft compiled to a guest, the Godot build service, the MCP guest, the private org's double-engine repository). b: State: discussion Scope: weftspun-bao and the weftspun-fdb machines it runs on. Bao runs as three replicas, one beside each FDB machine. Bao was one machine, and every consumer now depends on it: every routine credential read, coordination write and policy check routes through Bao, so one outage stops them all. ha_enabled = true , coordinated over FDB (operator, 2026-10-13). The weftspun-bao app retires once the three instances serve. Superseded on 2026-11-01: Bao runs as one instance beside a single-node FDB cluster on one Fly machine, restored from the R2 backup, with ha_enabled = false (operator, 2026-11-01). Deploy the image to the three weftspun-fdb machines one at a time and unseal each, then destroy the weftspun-bao app once the three serve. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped. Why HA now, not before RFD66606-2140 chose ha_enabled = "false" when Bao was one machine and one operator. Under that arrangement, Bao being down meant one thing was down: the Bao API. Everything else routed around Bao by holding its credentials in Fly secrets or 1P. RFD66606-2146 turned that inside out. Every consumer now authenticates to Bao with its per-service cert, reads its credentials from Bao at runtime, and coordinates state through Bao's KV. When Bao goes down, the DNS-editing path goes down, the R2-write path goes down, the FDB coordinator info lookup goes down, and any new spend gate that follows the same pattern goes down with them. The single-machine posture that was fine as a convenience store is not fine as the switchboard. Colocated on the FDB machines The operator chose on 2026-10-13 to run Bao on the three weftspun-fdb machines instead of in its own app. The Fly plan in use includes three shared-cpu-1x 256 MB machines and 3 GB of volumes; three FDB machines plus a separate Bao machine overran both, and the separate machine bought no redundancy. FDB keeps double redundancy and three coordinators, so one machine may still be lost. Each machine runs fdbserver, the backup agent, Bao, tailscaled and sshd, at 512 MB. Measured on 2026-10-13 at 256 MB: an FDB machine used about 130 MB, and the Bao machine about 130 MB, of which Bao was 77 MB, tailscaled 26 MB and the plugin 18 MB. The two together do not fit in the 207 MB a 256 MB machine leaves usable. - The weftspun-bao app retires once the three instances serve. Its volume held no secrets: Bao's storage is FDB, and the volume kept the tailnet identity, the SSH host key and renewed listener certificates. - Each instance advertises its own machine address as api_addr and cluster_addr , so standbys forward to the active instance. Standbys forward every read to the active instance. - Clients keep verifying the listener as weftspun-bao.internal ; the name in the certificate does not move with the app. - One machine carries the existing tailnet state and keeps the weftspun-bao node; the others join under their own names. - The SSH tunnel port is balanced across all three machines, so they share one host key, held as a secret rather than generated per volume. - The change is proved on a throwaway three-machine app before weftspun-fdb is touched: an initialised test Bao, a secret written and read back, one machine restarted and unsealed while the others keep serving. Replicas: 3 in sjc, coordinated over FDB OpenBao's FDB backend supports HA by leader election over the same storage the writes go to. One instance runs on each FDB machine, so Bao spreads across the same three zones FDB does. Standby replicas can either serve reads directly or forward every request to the leader. Read-serving standbys would suit the read/write ratio the cert-auth path establishes (many reads per one write); until the fork is shown to serve reads from a standby, standbys forward. The 3-machine scale exposes one wrinkle: three machines mean three seal states, three unseal calls per fleet restart. This is the reason auto-unseal stays the goal. Migration path Enabling the replicas on the live cluster is: 1. Update service-openbao/config-fdb.hcl : ha_enabled = "true" . 2. Build one image carrying the FDB server and Bao, and deploy it to the three weftspun-fdb machines one at a time, unsealing each. 3. Stop the weftspun-bao app, then destroy it once the three serve. A desk reaches the active instance Read on 2026-10-16. The three instances elect one leader, and only the leader answers a login; a standby redirects to the leader's .vm.weftspun-fdb.internal address, which no desk resolves. Two of the three carried tailnet names that day ( weftspun-bao-3 , weftspun-bao-4 ), both unsealed standbys, and the leader, the third machine, had none, so a desk asking the tailnet found no leader and the desk helper exited without a word. The route that worked: read sys/leader from any instance (no token, mTLS only), take the machine id out of leader_address , and run fly proxy 8200:8200 .vm.weftspun-fdb.internal -a weftspun-fdb as a background process. The desk then uses BAO_ADDR=https://127.0.0.1:8200 with BAO_TLS_SERVER_NAME=weftspun-bao.internal and its agent certificate. The proxy exits on its own after some minutes; a connection refused on 127.0.0.1:8200 means restart it, not that Bao is down. The retired weftspun-bao app still exists, stopped. fly proxy -a weftspun-bao fails with host was not found in DNS because nothing runs there, and starting its machine brings up a second Bao against the same FDB storage, which stops again within a minute. It was started twice that day by mistake before the route above was found; it is not started again, and its deletion is an open item. Sub-decisions open - Delete the retired weftspun-bao app and its volume, so a desk cannot start a second Bao by mistake. - Every instance joins the tailnet under its own name, or the leader's name is published where a desk can read it without a Fly login. - 3 replicas, one per FDB machine (operator, 2026-10-13). - Standbys serve reads ( disable_performance_standby = false ) vs forward to leader. Read-heavy workload argues for serving. - The FDB and Bao data machines run as one machine or as an HA set; the one-machine form relies on tested backups (operator, 2026-10-30). Sources - OpenBao HA storage docs (FDB backend supports HA via leader election on the shared FDB cluster). - RFD66606-2140 (Bao on FDB, this raises its ambition), 2145 (leaf and CA rotation cadence this HA has to survive), 2146 (the capability topology this now underwrites). The problem RFD66606-2140's ha_enabled = "false" fit that framing. RFD66606-2146 then moved every routine credential read, coordination write, and policy check onto Bao. Every consumer now depends on Bao being up, and RFD66606-2140's reliability budget is smaller than what routes through Bao now needs. The tuples rebac rfd-2353--provides--bao-single-fly-instance rfd-2353--is-a--deployment rfd-2353--spends--bao rfd-2353--spends--bao-fdb-storage-backend rfd-2353--spends--bao-cert-auth-role-map rfd-2353--spends--fdb-backup-r2-dr-tag rfd-2353--spends--fly rfd-2353--spends--tailscale Related RFD66606-2140, RFD66606-2144, RFD66606-2145, RFD66606-2146. Split from the old RFD66606-2147: RFD66606-2354 (unseal), 2355 (cache), 2356 (no CDN proxy).

b: State: discussion Scope: the seal of every Bao, its key, and its recovery. Bao restarts and unseals with no person at the keyboard. Three Baos mean three seal states and three unseal calls per fleet restart. A transit seal on a Seal Bao on Fly, unwrapped from Fly KMS at boot (operator, 2026-10-30). Recovery becomes hands-off, not operator-with-1P. Superseded on 2026-11-01: Bao runs as one Fly machine and unseals from Fly KMS at boot, with an offline division of the seal key with n=1 as the last resort (operator, 2026-11-01). Pass the recovery test on clean hosts before prod moves; the sections below hold the steps. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped. Auto-unseal: KMS wrapper, Shamir stays as break-glass Shamir with a manual share is the right seal for one-of-one, wrong for three-of-three. Options: - Cloud KMS seal (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, Oracle). The key stays in the cloud KMS; Bao decrypts the master key at boot via the KMS API. Standard pattern. Cost is per-request against the KMS, measured in fractions of a cent per unseal. - Transit seal (a second, seed-only Bao). Chicken-and-egg unless the seed Bao is truly offline (Raspberry Pi, HSM, boot-from-USB). Adds a second thing to maintain. - HSM / PKCS 11 . Right answer for a fleet in a datacenter with its own HSM. Overkill for this workspace's scale. - HCP Vault / OpenBao managed . Not this workspace's shape. Recommendation: Fly KMS, through a Seal Bao. Fly app secret keys are a first-party KMS, usable only from inside a machine of the owning app, and OpenBao has no Fly seal type, so a Seal Bao bridges the two (operator, 2026-10-30). The break-glass key for the day the KMS itself is the outage (the day RFD66606-2144 logs as its eleventh defect) is the Seal Bao's static key, held offline as a Shamir share, whose count may be 1. An auto-unseal wrapper does not change the CRL-loop bug logged during the DR (Bao's authenticated paths going flaky after a particular sequence of issuer imports). That is a separate item. Transit seal on Fly, unwrapped by Fly KMS The operator chose on 2026-10-13 to unseal the Fly instances from a small Bao, rescinded the Mac mini as its host on 2026-10-30, and chose a Seal Bao on Fly that unwraps its own key from Fly KMS (operator, 2026-10-30). - Encrypt and decrypt with a Fly secret key work only from inside a machine of the owning app, through the machine's local API socket; the public API refuses. The Seal Bao's start-up script decrypts a wrapped 32-byte key into memory and starts Bao with a static seal. Every other Bao uses a stock transit seal against it. - The Seal Bao runs as one machine or as an HA set of three voters. Two voters tolerate no failure, so two is not a valid setting (operator, 2026-10-30). One machine relies on a restore from backup that has been tested. - It listens only on its tailnet address, over TLS, and the tailnet policy lets only Bao nodes reach it. No peer reaches a localhost or public listener. - Each Bao has its own transit key and a policy limited to encrypt and decrypt on that key. A certificate login yields a short token, but a seal needs its token at boot, so each Bao also holds a periodic orphan token for its key: a Fly secret on the Fly instances, a file readable only by its own user elsewhere. Measured on a throwaway Bao, the seal renews that token while the Bao runs; the token expires if the Bao is down longer than its period, so the period is set to days and a longer outage needs a new token. - If the Seal Bao is down, a restarted Bao stays sealed until it is back. Running Baos keep serving. - The break-glass key is the Seal Bao's static key, held offline as a Shamir share even when the count is 1, and never in the backup bucket. A new Seal Bao started with that key and a restored snapshot unlocks every other Bao. Each Bao's Shamir recovery keys authorise operations such as generating a root token; they do not unseal. - The Seal Bao backs up to the same bucket as the others, under its own prefix, with unique object names and a retention lock; plain-text config files stay out of the snapshots and are protected separately. - The change is proved with a planted control: with the Seal Bao stopped, a restarted Bao stays sealed. The recovery test passes before prod moves: on clean hosts with Fly blocked, restore the Seal Bao from the offline key and the backup, then restore one other Bao through it and read back data. Recovery without Fly KMS This procedure needs no Fly account, no Fly machine and no network path to Fly. It is the one the recovery test runs (operator, 2026-10-30). 1. Gather the materials: the offline Shamir share or shares of the Seal Bao's static key, the Seal Bao's configuration without its secrets, and the newest snapshot of the Seal Bao from the backup bucket. 2. Rebuild the key: combine the shares into the 32-byte key (one share is the key itself). Check the length and the key id the configuration names before use. 3. Start a new Seal Bao on any host with a static seal whose key is a file in memory backed storage, and with the same listener rules: tailnet address, TLS. 4. Restore the snapshot into it. Whether the restore needs the force option under a fresh barrier is not yet measured; the recovery test settles it. 5. Check that the transit keys, the policies and the cert roles are back, and that one other Bao unseals through the new address with its existing periodic token. 6. Point the other Baos at the new address if it changed, one at a time. 7. Resume hands-off unsealing by wrapping the key with a new KMS, or by leaving it manual until one exists. A Bao that stays up needs none of this; only a restart does. 8. Write down what the restore took and which step was unclear, then amend this block. The key never leaves the offline store except during steps 2 and 3, and the memory copy is destroyed when the host stops. Alternative wrapper: a passkey Fly KMS is the hands-off wrapper. A passkey can wrap the same 32-byte static key when no Fly KMS is available, at the price of a person at every restart (operator, 2026-10-30). The route has not been run here; the recovery test measures it. - Passkey. A passkey whose authenticator offers a secret-derivation extension can derive a wrapping key from a challenge, with a touch. Support differs by authenticator and by client library, so confirm that the same credential returns the same secret on a second host before relying on it. A passkey that only signs cannot wrap anything. - Hardware seal in Bao. OpenBao can seal through a PKCS 11 module, but that needs a token that decrypts or unwraps with a mechanism the seal supports; whether a passkey does is not known. Until measured, the passkey wraps the static key and Bao keeps its static seal. - Keep two passkeys, stored apart, since one lost token otherwise ends recovery. A passkey stays out of the backup bucket and off any Fly host. How the key arrives, and rotating the seal A Bao on a static seal holds one 32-byte key. How that key reaches the process is a mode in the start-up script, not part of the seal. Every mode supplies the same key, so a node changes mode with no migration (operator, 2026-10-30). - tpm : a non-exportable TPM key unwraps a wrapped copy of the key at start, with no PIN and no touch. The wrapped file opens only on that machine. - kms : the start-up script asks the Seal Bao, or on Fly the machine's own KMS, for the key. - passkey : a person touches the passkey at each start. - manual : the script asks a person for the key, for example from the offline Shamir shares, and then starts Bao. Bao does not start without the key, and a static seal has no manual unseal of its own. A node left in this mode starts nothing on its own. - A node lists the modes it has in order and uses the first that works, for example tpm , then kms , then passkey , then manual . Each node wraps the key once per mode it lists, so any one is enough (operator, 2026-10-30). The script logs which mode unwrapped the key, so a fallback shows. Splitting the key so that several modes are all required is not used: one broken mode would then block the start. - The plain key is held in memory-backed storage only for the start, and the file is deleted once Bao reports unsealed. - Changing the seal type is a different act: it is seal key rotation, run with bao operator unseal -migrate while the old seal still answers, and it needs a restart. Measured on the operator's desktop on 2026-10-30, a TPM 2.0 firmware TPM: a 32-byte key wrapped to a non-exportable key unwrapped to the same bytes; a changed byte in the wrapped file, an export of the private key and a deleted key were each refused. A Bao with a static seal fed by that unwrap initialised, restarted and unsealed with nobody typing, and a wrong key left it sealed. Not measured: a reboot, a copy of the wrapped file on another machine, and the kms , passkey and manual modes. The Steam Deck shows a TPM 2.0 device that systemd-creds cannot use without root; the Steam Frame is unchecked. Migration to the transit seal Stand up the Seal Bao on Fly and pass its recovery test, add a seal "transit" block to the Fly config, and migrate with one last Shamir unseal ( -migrate ). The Shamir key stays offline as the recovery key. Sub-decisions open - The seal provider: a Seal Bao on Fly, unwrapped from Fly KMS (operator, 2026-10-30). - Whether the Seal Bao runs as one machine or as three voters; both are allowed. - Where the offline copy of the Seal Bao's key is kept. - Whether to write the CRL-loop fix (a separate bug) into this rollout or before it. Sources - Vault auto-unseal precedent for the KMS wrapper pattern ( cloud kms auto-unseal , applies unchanged to OpenBao forks). - RFD66606-2144 (its eleventh defect: the without-auto-unseal failure mode). The problem Bao was one machine, Shamir seal single share, operator+1P recovery per restart. Shamir with a manual share is the right seal for one-of-one, wrong for three-of-three. Related RFD66606-2144, RFD66606-2145, RFD66606-2146. Split from the old RFD66606-2147: RFD66606-2353 (replicas), 2355 (cache), 2356 (no CDN proxy).
t: RFD66606-2354: Bao unseals itself through a Seal Bao on Fly

b: State: discussion Scope: every consumer of Bao: DNS, R2 writes, FDB coordinator lookup. A consumer that holds a bearer for a few minutes keeps Bao out of its critical path. Every read against Bao is a Bao dependency, and DNS, R2 writes and the FDB coordinator lookup all read from it. Consumers cache what they can. A bearer held for a few minutes puts Bao in the critical path only at cache expiry. Check a consumer that reads Bao against the rule above: it caches the value in its own memory for less time than the value protects, and on a Bao error it retries rather than holding the stale value. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped. Consumer-side cache: what and for how long Every read against Bao is a Bao dependency. Two ends of the spectrum: - Never cache. Simple, correct, hot dependency on Bao. - Cache forever. Wrong for rotating secrets (RFD66606-2145 leaves at 90 days; a hot bearer at hour 720 leaks past its rotation). The middle: cache for a duration shorter than the shortest thing the cached value protects. For a DNS bearer that itself has a Cloudflare API-token lifetime, minutes-to-an-hour is safe. For an FDB cluster file that changes only on a scale event, an hour is safe. Cache should live in the CONSUMER's memory, not on disk, and it should refresh on a Bao error by simply retrying rather than by holding the stale value. The problem RFD66606-2146 moved every routine credential read onto Bao, so every consumer now depends on Bao being up. Related RFD66606-2145, RFD66606-2146. Split from the old RFD66606-2147: RFD66606-2353 (replicas), 2354 (unseal), 2356 (no CDN proxy).
t: RFD66606-2355: Consumers cache Bao reads in memory

b: State: discussion Scope: the DNS records of every workspace service. Workspace services stay DNS-only, so no CDN reads their traffic. A proxied record puts Cloudflare between a client and the service for every request. CF-proxied records have Cloudflare terminating TLS at its edge, every byte plaintext at CF for the round trip. Workspace services stay DNS-only; edge cache, if needed, is Fly-side or origin-side. If a workspace service lands under a proxied subdomain, take the proxy flag off before it serves requests. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped. No CDN proxy in front of workspace services Cloudflare's proxied: true mode has CF terminating TLS at its edge using its Universal SSL cert and re-encrypting to origin. Every byte of the request headers and body is plaintext at CF for the round trip. CF is not the workspace's tenant. That is a MITM regardless of intent, and it is not compatible with services that carry auth tokens or hostname-bound credentials. Records for services this workspace runs stay proxied: false . Edge caching, if it is ever needed, lives Fly-side (Fly's own Anycast + edge) or origin-side (an in-process cache). One record in the chibifire.com zone as of 2026-09-01 is CF-proxied: hub-700a.chibifire.com , pointing at 173.180.240.105 / 2001:569:7e58:dd00:... . That is a personal home network endpoint, outside this workspace's scope. If a workspace service ever lands under a subdomain that is currently proxied, the proxy flag comes off before the service starts serving requests. The problem Services here carry auth tokens and hostname-bound credentials. Related RFD66606-2146. Split from the old RFD66606-2147: RFD66606-2353 (replicas), 2354 (unseal), 2355 (cache).
t: RFD66606-2356: Workspace services stay DNS-only

b: State: discussion Feature: numeric precision for kernels on float32 and bf16 units Scope: df32 guest geometry, and f32 matrix products on bf16 units such as a TPU. A narrow unit gives wide precision when each number is split into parts it can hold. A float32 coordinate 3.8e8 m from the origin cannot hold a 1 mm step, and a bf16 unit holds 8 bits of mantissa. A TPU computes a float32 product as 3 or 6 bf16 passes. A df32 pair computes a wide coordinate as a high and a low float32. Both split a number into a sum of narrow parts. 1. A kernel that needs more precision than its unit holds splits the operands into parts and sums the products of the parts, smallest first. 2. A kernel states its part count: 1, 2 or 3 bf16 parts, or one df32 pair. 3. Each part count carries a measured error against a float64 reference, and a control that fails when the count drops by one. Record the measured error of a kernel before it claims float32 or df32 accuracy. This RFD was drafted by an AI and read by a human before it shipped. What the TPU library states The array library that drives Cloud TPU documents its matrix precision setting in its source, read from the main branch at the time of writing. The setting changes float32 computations only and leaves the input and output types alone. - DEFAULT : on TPU, float32 computations run in bfloat16. - HIGH : on TPU, float32 computations run in 3 bfloat16 passes. - HIGHEST : on TPU, float32 computations run in 6 bfloat16 passes. The dot algorithm presets name the same idea: BF16_BF16_F32_X3 , BF16_BF16_F32_X6 and BF16_BF16_F32_X9 use 3, 6 and 9 operations to emulate higher precision, and a float8 preset decomposes each operand into an initial term and a residual term. The source does not state which products the 3 and 6 pass modes keep, and no TPU ran for this RFD. The host measurement below chooses the usual split: 2 parts keep the 3 products whose part indexes sum to at most 1, 3 parts keep the 6 whose indexes sum to at most 2, and 9 keeps all products of 3 parts. The split rule A part is the operand rounded to bf16. The residual is the operand minus the part, exact in float32. The next part is the residual rounded to bf16, and so on. Three bf16 parts hold 3 times 8 bits, which covers the 24 bit float32 mantissa. A product of two bf16 values is exact in float32. The sum of the kept products runs in float32, smallest products first, so the large products do not drown the small ones. df32 is the same split one level up. Error is the norm of the difference from a float64 product, over the norm of that product. Median over the seeds, with the maximum in brackets. product K = 256 K = 4096 1 bf16 part 2.3e-3 (2.4e-3) 2.4e-3 (2.4e-3) 3 products, 2 parts (X3) 4.4e-6 (4.6e-6) 4.4e-6 (4.6e-6) 6 products, 3 parts (X6) 9.6e-8 (9.9e-8) 1.2e-7 (1.2e-7) 9 products, 3 parts (X9) 9.6e-8 (9.9e-8) 1.2e-7 (1.2e-7) float32 host product 2.5e-7 (2.6e-7) 2.4e-7 (2.4e-7) Each step up the table lowers the error, from 2.3e-3 to 1.2e-7 over three steps. b: State: discussion Scope: how the Sakuragaoka Station port builds, shades and renders its geometry in Godot. The station port draws baked meshes in Godot, so it renders with the runtime vector shader off. CSG keeps UV and drops vertex colour, and it takes only manifold solids, so a geometry that fails the manifold check cannot be unioned as it is. The Sakuragaoka Station port ( entities-sakuragaoka-station ( 4-entities/sakuragaoka-station )): - realizes every closed solid through CSG, and carries each face's colour as a palette index in UV, since CSG keeps UV and drops vertex colour. CSG takes only manifold solids, so a geometry that fails the manifold check stays a plain surface, or goes through remesh.elf when it must be unioned; - shades with godot-vrm's MToon unchanged, and a variant includes it rather than forking it; - renders from meshes baked from the vector materials' data (signs, paving, bark), coarsened by LOD when over budget, so it works with the runtime vector shader off. Alpha-cut foliage cards bake too: each blossom card is its atlas cell's outline, baked by slug.elf at 256 triangles a cell, and the cards go into cluster LOD DAGs built by remesh.elf 's cluster_lod (meshoptimizer's clusterlod.h ), which clod_select cuts per frame, binary-translated, on both standalone headsets (operator, 2026-10-10); - judges alpha on the final composite of its layers: an opaque object ends with no transparency, and a transparent base-colour material writes alpha. Check a new station mesh against the rule: realize each closed solid through CSG, bake vector materials to meshes, and keep rasterized vector art out of the headset. Quality and procedural detail The Sakuragaoka Station port: - runs slughorn 's per-pixel vector shader as a quality setting, on by default, adding detail to surfaces near the eye within the headset's GPU budget; - synthesizes finer detail only where the source is procedural. What stays out of the headset No rasterized vector art or glyph outline goes into the headset. Meshes made from outlines are fine, and a glyph mesh goes through remesh.elf when its font's winding is invalid. The blossom cards and the cut Over the 48 valid orbit views, the 53,211 cards are 13.6M triangles at full detail, and a 4 px cut for a 1760 px eye at 100 degrees draws a mean of 39k and at most 122k. With the cut, depth differs from the original on 0.16 % of the frame, and on 2.15 % without the cards. Translated, the cut takes a median 1.6 ms a view on the desk, and 4.3 ms interpreted. The outline The outline reads the mesh's geometric normal, which the toon-ramp hook writes, not MToon's bent indirect-light normal, and takes depth and normal from the majority MSAA sample.
